articles.title: The 13 Most Outrageous New Dishes At NFL Stadiums Across The Country
articles.summary: NFL stadiums are serving wild new foods for the 2026 season, including giant hot dogs, loaded burgers, crab-stuffed pretzels and two-foot quesadillas.
articles.body:
It's football season , baby! Sure, I don't follow the sport, but I do follow the food. I'm all in for football Sundays at the local sports bar, tailgating, and most importantly, trying all the new and ridiculous dishes stadiums dream up each season.

While I'm still not sure what a first down is or the difference between zone and man-to-man coverage, I do know that you can't watch a game without an order of chicken wings by your side.

And stadiums across the country are pulling out all the stops this year when it comes to their food selections. From two-foot-long hot dogs to colossal burgers, here are some of the wildest things football fans can eat this season.

New in the suites this year are these fanciful Crab Cake Sliders featuring Northeastern-style crab cakes, Hartwell's citrus ranch remoulade, and locally sourced bacon relish, all piled on Turano Baking Co. brioche buns.

Arrowhead, home turf for Mr. Taylor Swift himself, Travis Kelce, isn't messing around with its burgers this season. The Lava Burger is a cheese-stuffed patty topped with thick-cut bacon, roasted tomato, chives, and jalapeño popper spread, all served on a sourdough boule. You can find it in Section 102.

Lincoln Financial Field—Philadelphia Eagles

In Philly, it's all about the tush push. This year, fans in the East and West Club Markets can order the Tush Push Tater, a deep-fried russet potato topped with fried chicken cutlet, pimento mac and cheese, bacon hot honey jam, 215 sauce, and scallions. My mouth is already watering.

Empower Field At Mile High—Denver Broncos

Can you tame the beast? Broncos fans can try their luck with the Beast in a Blanket, a two-foot dog loaded with brisket burnt ends, cheddar, and goat cheese, then wrapped in puff pastry and topped with avocado cream, crispy onions, jalapeño, and secret sauce. You can find the $45 behemoth in Section 128.

Looking for something colorful? The Battle Red Berry Bird features fried chicken tossed in strawberry buffalo sauce and topped with coleslaw, pickles, and Cajun cheese curds. It's served on a challah bun with Tater Kegs and chipotle aioli, and you can find it in Sections 101, 121, 520, and 546.

If you're particularly hungry in Section 150, order the Who Dey Sausage . The 24-inch BBQ cheddar pork sausage comes piled with pickled red onions, fresh jalapeño, and sweet BBQ sauce.

At Hungry Dawg Grill in Section 118, fans can order a Hot Dog Flight featuring three very different mini dogs.

There's the Buffalo Blitz Dog, which comes topped with Buffalo chicken dip, celery, blue cheese crumbles, and Buffalo sauce. The Italian Stallion piles on spaghetti, chopped meatballs, marinara, Parmesan, and fresh basil, while the Brisket Dog is loaded with smoked brisket, fried onions, pickles, bourbon BBQ sauce, and Gouda.

Rep your team with Acrisure Stadium's new Black N' Gold Chicken and Waffle, available in the PNC Champions Club. The dish features house-made black-and-gold waffles topped with fried chicken, coleslaw, bacon jam, sweet potato fries, and Mike's Hot Honey. Talk about a mouthful!

This might be one of the most genius combinations since peanut butter and jelly. Northwest Stadium's Crab Stuffed Pretzel is exactly what it sounds like: a crab-shaped pretzel filled with lemon-tarragon crab dip, brushed with garlic butter and finished with grated Parmesan cheese.

Fans of da Bears can get their hands on the Bear-ia Burrito, filled with shredded beef birria, Chihuahua cheese, cilantro, and onion, then served with house-made consommé.

Lions fans can order the Corktown Corned Beef Nachos, made with fresh kettle chips, corned beef, white cheese sauce, Thousand Island dressing, coleslaw, tomato, and chives.

Bank of America Stadium—Carolina Panthers

If you consider yourself a Panther groupie, the Big 'Dilla has your name on it. This two-foot smoked adobo chicken monster quesadilla is packed with cheddar and Jack cheese and pico de gallo, then finished with cilantro and chipotle crema.

Head to Section 101 or 328 to get your hands on The Raid Burger. The monster-sized handheld features a double bacon cheeseburger topped with Buffalo cheese curds, an onion ring, and ranch on a brioche bun.

articles.title: Saints vs Lions and Cardinals vs Chargers form the ideal football betting teaser combination
articles.summary: A Saints vs. Lions and Cardinals vs. Chargers NFL teaser pairs Detroit at -1 with Los Angeles at -3.5 for a combined bet line at an attractive -135 odds.
articles.body: In basically any other sport, you really only bet on sides, totals, player props, and parlays. That doesn’t mean that there is a lack of options – there are hundreds, if not thousands, of betting options available to you every day that the four major sports are active. But, with NFL football, we also have teasers that we can invest in. Let’s get to it with these two picks: Saints vs. Lions, 1 pm ET The New Orleans Saints are in a winnable division. They don’t even need to be great to do it, which is good because they probably won’t be great. The team has some talent on it, but they aren’t one that you’ll mistake for a Super Bowl contender. The team has Tyler Shough entering his second year under center. Travis Etienne Jr. came over from Jacksonville and makes the backfield a bit younger. Chris Olave is still a talented receiver, but he does have Shough throwing to him. The defense is still a bit questionable, but similar to the offense – there is talent, but seeing how it comes together will be the biggest challenge. NEW ORLEANS SAINTS PROJECTED UNDER 5.5 WINS AS ROSTER TRANSITION CONTINUES INTO 2026 SEASON The Detroit Lions don’t have nearly as many issues or concerns going into this season. They had a bit of a down year last year, ending 9-8. There were some really impressive moments, and others that looked a bit rough. The team comes in with a dynamic offense that should rack up points. The defense will be a question in comparison. I’m a bit higher on them than others. I think Aidan Hutchinson will be great again, and Derrick Moore could be a good complement. The first leg of the teaser is to take the Lions from -7 to -1. This essentially only means we need to get the Lions to win the game. If they win by one, it is a push, but I think they should win this one by three or more at home with the better offense and a better defense. There isn’t really an aspect of this game the Lions have a disadvantage in. LIONS BETTING OUTLOOK FOR 2025: WHY THE NFC NORTH DIVISION TITLE IS THE BEST PLAY AT +170 Cardinals vs. Chargers, 4:25 ET The Arizona Cardinals are coming into this year as one of the worst teams in football. Their roster is pieced together with virtually anyone they can grab. That isn’t to say they have no good players. Jeremiyah Love is a really good running back and could be the most exciting person on the offense. However, he has a high ankle sprain, so he might not get in this one at all. Trey McBride is elite as a receiving option, but Marvin Harrison Jr. looks like he could be a bust. There isn’t much to speak of on defense, either. They have one of the worst-ranked defensive lines in football according to PFF. CAN MARVIN HARRISON JR. AND TREY MCBRIDE CARRY THE CARDINALS OFFENSE UNDER NEW COACH MIKE LAFLEUR? The Los Angeles Chargers are one of the better teams in football, and I think this could be a big year for them. The Chargers are well-coached and have a strong defense. The question might actually be around the offense because Justin Herbert is now with Mike McDonald. How, and how quickly, they mesh will be an intriguing part of this season. I still think the Chargers have a high floor on both sides of the ball. This game is one the Chargers should win even if most things go wrong for them. Jacoby Brissett has had some really nice games for them, but this Chargers defense will have the correct schemes to battle him. I’m going to take the Chargers down to -3.5 on the teaser line. EX-NFL STAR BELIEVES MIKE MCDANIEL'S 'BEST DECISION OF HIS CAREER' WAS JOINING CHARGERS WITH JUSTIN HERBERT This combination of Chargers -3.5 and Lions -1, gets you one bet at -135. If you want to push the lines to Chargers -3 and Lions -0.5, you can get the bet at -143. Your call, but I think these games should see comfortable wins from both teams. articles.title: Raiders favored at -3 over Miami Dolphins as Malik Willis and Kirk Cousins face off in NFL week one
articles.summary: The first full Red Zone schedule features the Miami Dolphins vs. Las Vegas Raiders, and in a home game, the Raiders at -3 look like the smart betting play.
articles.body: I wish I had an opening line that was memorable like Scott Hanson over on Red Zone. There isn’t anything I can write that will provide the same level of excitement that "7 hours of commercial-free football" gives. That’s what is on the horizon for us, though. We have hours of uninterrupted football, and our first full schedule. My first play of the weekend comes as the Dolphins take on the Raiders. The Miami Dolphins are my pick to earn something really special this year… the #1 overall draft pick. That’s not exactly a good sign, but I do think they will be the worst team in football. The Dolphins team has been decimated over the course of the past year. Their coach from last season: gone. Their starting quarterback from last season: gone. Their top wide receivers (Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle): gone and gone. Is there any hope for optimism in this game? De’Von Achane is still one of the better running backs in the game. Malik Willis is dynamic and has shown flashes of success in both Tennessee and Green Bay. At the same time, Achane might not have any running space considering the teams know he is the best and only true threat on the team. Willis has shown flashes, but he has also shown that he is normally a backup quarterback for a reason. MIAMI DOLPHINS ENTER FULL REBUILD WITH MALIK WILLIS AT QUARTERBACK AND JEFF HAFLEY AS HEAD COACH The Las Vegas Raiders also underwent many changes this offseason. They earned the #1 overall pick last year with a terrible season of their own. That saw them dismiss Pete Carroll and bring in Klint Kubiak to take over the franchise. It also saw them select Fernando Mendoza with the first pick, and then they also grabbed Kirk Cousins, who worked with Kubiak previously. The Raiders tried to trade away Maxx Crosby in the offseason, but that was vetoed, and he is now back on the roster. He should still be solid for the club, but there are questions around the rest of the defense. Their new coach is also not a defensive guy, so there is reason to be concerned about this side of the ball. For some context, the Raiders are ranked 24th in the league for defensive line rankings. The Dolphins are 30th. Brock Bowers is out for the game, and that hurts the Raiders, but I think it will be okay against the Dolphins. KIRK COUSINS AND NO 1 PICK FERNANDO MENDOZA GIVE RAIDERS BETTORS SOME HOPE IN THE UPCOMING YEAR We have two quarterbacks in new spots, and questionable defenses. Does that mean we will get a high-scoring game, or will the quarterbacks be too busy trying to figure things out? Personally, I think we get the higher-scoring game, but I’m not touching the total. I don’t think there is enough on one side or the other to really invest in it. I do lean toward the over 40.5, though. Instead, I’m backing the Raiders at -3 in this one. Las Vegas is one of the teams that I think will improve, but let’s not believe that they will win a ton of games. They are still going to miss the playoffs. There are still a lot of questions. But for one game, the Raiders should win the game by at least three points, and I think they should win by five or more. Back the Raiders. articles.title: Week 1 NFL odds, picks, predictions: Our best bets, including a play in Cowboys-Giants
articles.summary: Our NFL handicappers give out their favorite bets for Week 1 games.
articles.body:
Week 1 of the NFL began with a 13-10 Seattle Seahawks win over the New England Patriots and continued on Thursday night with the NFL's first-ever regular season game played in Australia — a 27-7 victory by the San Francisco 49ers over the Los Angeles Rams .

What will the rest of the weekend have in store for bettors?

Our NFL handicapping team of Corbie Craig, Matt Jacob, Jeremy Pond and Matt Russell combine to give their best bets for Week 1 of the NFL season.

Jacob: The highest total on the Week 1 NFL slate comes from Cincinnati — and it makes complete sense. After all, the Bengals' defense leaked like a broken water main all last season, while Tampa Bay 's stop unit was well below average. Also, the two quarterbacks in this contest — Baker Mayfield and Joe Burrow — are big-armed veterans who combined for 43 touchdown passes in just 25 games in 2025.

Here's what you may not know: Burrow is a notorious slow starter. He has one total touchdown pass in the last three season openers. And for his career, he has many interceptions (five) as TD throws in Week 1.

Now check out Cincinnati's points production in its six openers this decade: 17 (vs. Cleveland last year); 10 (vs. New England in 2024); 3 (at Cleveland in 2023); 20 (vs. Pittsburgh in overtime in 2022); 27 (vs. Minnesota in overtime in 2021); 13 (vs. the Chargers in 2020). Only the game against the Vikings (27-24 final) hurdled 43 combined points.

To be fair, Mayfield has been spectacular in his three openers with Tampa Bay (nine TDs, zero INTs). However, only one of the Buccaneers' last four Week 1 games has cleared 43 points.

Then there's this: Since 2022, seven Week 1 contests have closed with a total of at least 50 points. Only twice did the over cash.

Jacob: Minnesota followed up its stunning 14-3 record in 2024 with a miserable start to last season, dropping eight of the first dozen games. Rather than throw in the towel, though, the Vikings regrouped and closed on a five-game winning streak to finish one game above .500. And they did it with J.J. McCarthy — now the team's third-string QB — starting four of the five contests.

Meanwhile, the 2025 Packers went the complete opposite direction, dropping their final four games after a 9-3-1 start to miss the playoffs for just the second time in seven years.

Obviously, there's no certainty that late-season momentum — either positive or negative — will carry over to this year. But at least the Vikings' roster is in better shape: Minnesota enters the season without a single starter on the injured list. Conversely, Green Bay won't have ineligible running back Josh Jacobs (whose backups are completely unproven); three starting offensive lineman are banged up (and that unit lost two of last year's starters to free agency); star pass-rusher Micah Parsons (torn Achilles) is on IR; and two starting defensive linemen are questionable.

What about new Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray ? I believe he'll be a huge upgrade over McCarthy — in large part because I expect head coach Kevin O'Connell to resurrect Murray in the same way he did Sam Darnold two years ago.

Pond: We are about to experience the Justin Jefferson bounce-back season and it starts against the Packers in this NFC North showdown.

The two-time, First-team All-Pro wide receiver is coming off a campaign he'd surely like to forget. Jefferson finished with career lows in yards (1,048), average yards per catch (12.5) and touchdowns (two) for a Minnesota team that went 9-8 and missed the playoffs.

A season removed from that disappointment, Jefferson will get things cooking with Murray under center against a Green Bay defense missing Parsons.

Jump on this ladder play featuring four wagers, and which includes three at plus money. You can tack on over 110 yards (+310) if you're looking to go even deeper on these bets.

Bet: Jefferson alt receiving yards — 70+ Yards (-136) | 80+ Yards (+110) | 90+ Yards (+158) | 100+ Yards (+225) at FanDuel

Craig: Kenneth Walker III is walking into a crowded room in a new offense, in September, with a quarterback who has never handed him the ball in a game that counted. He ran for 1,027 yards on 221 carries across all 17 games for Seattle last season, which comes out to 60.4 yards a game, and the market has posted 61.5. That is last year's rate copied forward with a rounding error on top, and last year Walker was splitting a backfield in Seattle. He is not doing that now.

Kansas City signed him on March 12 to a three-year deal worth up to $45 million with $28.7 million guaranteed, and the Chiefs signed him to replace both Isiah Pacheco and Kareem Hunt . You don't pay a running back like that to hand him the same workload he had somewhere else.

Our projection lands at 67.9 yards and the case is volume rather than efficiency. A back getting 13 carries a game in a duo now should be getting more than that as the highest-paid piece of a Kansas City backfield that has lost its two most-used players.

Bet: Kenneth Walker III over 61.5 rushing yards (-109)

Craig: James Cook carried the ball 309 times in the regular season last year (18.2 attempts per game). He has been one of the most durable high-volume backs in football, and the market has him at 17.5 carries, which is a perfectly reasonable place to put a number for a back nobody has any reason to doubt. The problem with copying that number forward is that the man who called those plays is now the man running the team.

Offensive coordinator Joe Brady was promoted to head coach on Jan. 27 after Sean McDermott was fired, and Brady has already said publicly that Cook's workload was high and that the backfield needs to share it, with Ray Davis lined up behind him. That is not a beat writer's speculation — it's the head coach describing his own plan.

Then look at the opponent, because Houston fielded the best defense in football last season and then spent the whole offseason making the front even harder to run at, signing Logan Hall in free agency and trading up in the second round for Ohio State defensive tackle Kayden McDonald.

The last time these two teams played, Cook broke a 45-yard touchdown in the first quarter and then spent the rest of the afternoon grinding out 71 yards on his other 16 carries in a 23-19 Houston win, finishing with 17 attempts, which is under the number the market is asking you to lay today.

Bet: Cook under 17.5 rush attempts (-111)

Russell : It's Week 1, and we've already seen a star quarterback not make it out of the first series of the game, but the Falcons' quarterback situation looks to have that beat. Here are Atlanta's options to start at QB for a road game on Sunday:

Michael Penix — not ready to return from an ACL injury.

Tua Tagovailoa — already rumored to be on the chopping block barring epic performance, tumbled to the ground with a back issue in Thursday's practice.

Cooper Rush — four interceptions, no touchdowns on 52 attempts last season.

Jack Strand — undrafted free agent from Division II, Minnesota State-Moorhead.

Not to sound overly dramatic, but if the Steelers can't win this game by a touchdown or more, they should be eliminated from playoff contention.

The Falcons come into the season rated in the market as a below-average team (40 out of 100 in THE WINDOW 's estimated market ratings), but teams with quarterback debacles often see their rating for that week fall into the 20s. That would equate to a new line of Steelers -7, at least.

Pond: I'm expecting fireworks in this matchup of NFC East rivals who will shine on offense and struggle mightily on defense.

Dallas averaged 27.7 points per game a season ago, finishing second in total offense (6,663 yards) and seventh in points. In contrast, the Cowboys were downright atrocious on defense. They conceded a league-worst 30.1 PPG and wound up third in yards allowed (6,409) during a 7-9-1 campaign.

As for the Giants, they weren't much better on the defensive front. They finished 26th in team defense and yielded the fifth-worst yards (6,112) overall a season ago.

Sure, both franchises are optimistic they'll be able to turn things around, but I'm not buying it. These are teams that will be hard to stop when they have the ball and poor trying to defend.

Dallas and New York combined for a whopping 77 points in Week 2 of the 2025 campaign and 51 points in the rematch. I don't think we hit that gaudy number here, but clearing this total shouldn't be an issue.

articles.title: Steelers' Joey Porter Jr. reportedly unlikely to play Sunday amid back injury, contract dispute
articles.summary: Joey Porter Jr. reportedly won't play vs. the Falcons on Sunday.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is reportedly "unlikely" to play against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday as he deals with a back injury, according to multiple reports . Porter entered the weekend questionable with the injury.

Porter missed essentially all of training camp due to the issue. While Porter was activated from the physically unable to perform list Sept. 1 and has practiced, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy classifed Porter's work as a "ramp-up" after the cornerback missed so much time.

Despite getting in work during practice, Porter is not expected to go in Week 1. The injury, however, might not have anything to do with his situation. Porter has been seeking a new contract all summer, and talks have not resulted in a deal just yet.

Porter spoke openly about the issue the day he was activated, saying he wasn't sure if he would play in Week 1 if his contract situation was unresolved.

A week later, New England Patriots ' star cornerback Christian Gonzalez agreed to a massive four-year, $135 million extension with the team. That contract was expected to set the market for Porter, giving him a baseline for his next deal.

Despite that figure being out there, the Steelers and Porter still haven't agreed to a new contract.

While the Steelers have yet to confirm Porter's status for their Week 1 game against the Atlanta Falcons, the team dropped a significant hint Saturday that Porter would not play, elevating cornerback Doneiko Slaughter from the practice squad to the active roster .

It's unclear where Porter and the Steelers go from here. The team is reportedly open to trading the star cornerback, but is hoping to receive a first-round pick in a deal, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor. That cost has scared off potential trade partners, and no serious trade discussions have taken place just yet.

Porter has established himself as a strong player after being selected by the Steelers in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft. While he has yet to make the Pro Bowl in his first three NFL seasons, he's graded out well in Pro Football Focus' metrics.

The Steelers will undoubtedly miss Porter against the Falcons on Sunday. But unless the team's defense drastically falls apart without Porter, both sides could be looking at an extended absence for the time being.

articles.title: Malik Nabers' 'Murky' Injury Update Revealed in New NFL Rumors Ahead of Giants' Game vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: New York Giants fans reportedly may have to wait for Malik Nabers' season debut.
articles.body:
New York Giants fans reportedly may have to wait for Malik Nabers' season debut.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported ahead of Sunday night's game against the Dallas Cowboys that the wide receiver's "status is best described as murky at best. Very much up in the air for the New York Giants. It does not seem to me like something they are counting on."

The Giants seemed to be preparing for Nabers' potential absence when they elevated wide receivers Dalen Cambre and Braxton Berrios from the practice squad.

Rapoport described the moves as "insurance."

While Nabers did practice in full leading up to the game against the division-rival Cowboys, he is also coming off a torn ACL that limited him to just four games last season.

Earlier in training camp, the wide receiver took a long-term view on his recovery when asked whether he would be available for Week 1:

"The most important thing is my health," Nabers said. "The most important thing is just completing every milestone that they have in front of me, giving good effort, continuing to come out here and be a great teammate to my teammates."

Nabers is just 23 years old and surely expected to be a franchise cornerstone for years to come in New York. While having him on the field would elevate the team's chances against the Cowboys, there is more than just this game to consider when it comes to his return.

The LSU product wasted no time establishing himself as a star with 109 catches for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns as a rookie in 2024, and getting him back to that level for the foreseeable future will help the Giants once again become contenders in the NFC East after finishing with a losing record in eight of the last nine seasons.

It remains to be seen whether he will return to the field in Week 1, but even the chance he will be available suggests he will be back in the lineup in the near future.

articles.title: Malik Nabers remains questionable for Sunday Night Football vs. Cowboys, will 'let God tell me' if he's ready to play Week 1
articles.summary: Nabers hasn't played for the Giants since Week 4 of last year.
articles.body:
New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers remains questionable for Week 1's matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football" as he makes his return from a knee injury that ended his 2025 season after just four games.

Nabers practiced in full in the sessions leading up to season kickoff before being officially listed as questionable on the team's final injury report.

After Wednesday's practice, head coach John Harbaugh spoke to the media about Nabers' availability, saying, "I think he's ready to go," though it's been clear that they're taking Nabers' lead on how he's feeling and whether or not he'll be ready to play in Week 1.

When asked by reporters about when he'll know whether he can play on Sunday, Nabers said, "I'll let God tell me. Keeping my faith, and he'll let me know, and I'll know when it's time."

The Giants elevated wide receiver Braxton Berrios and signed wideout Dalen Cambre from the practice squad on Saturday ahead of Week 1, which could indicate the star will play limited snaps even if he is active, as the team bolsters its depth at the position.

Nabers is heading into the third season of his career. As a rookie in 2024, he finished fifth in Offensive Rookie of the Year voting after posting 1,204 yards with seven touchdowns.

There was a lot of hype around Nabers last season after the team drafted quarterback Jaxson Dart . Unfortunately, the Giants' top wide receiver tore his ACL in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers .

Before the injury, Nabers had played in four games and had 271 receiving yards and two touchdowns.

This year, a healthy Nabers is expected to lead the Giants' wide receiving corps. He should be Dart's top receiving threat if he is out there. Nabers will be joined by third-round pick Malachi Fields and veterans Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham Jr .

Nabers will look to bounce back in a big way in his 2026 season debut. He gets a familiar foe in the Cowboys, whom he has faced three times in his career. So far, Nabers has tallied 351 yards and two touchdowns on 29 receptions against New York's NFC East rival.

articles.title: Hits keep coming as Rams lose Myles Garrett for at least four games after looming knee surgery
articles.summary: Myles Garrett will undergo knee surgery and land on injured reserve, costing the Los Angeles Rams their prized acquisition for at least four games.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Rams had a great offseason but the start of the regular season has been a disaster and Myles Garrett needing knee surgery is perhaps the worst part of that. The Rams will be placing their signature offseason acquisition and 2025 Defensive Player of the Year on injured reserve, a source confirmed to OutKick. That means Garrett, who missed considerable practice time during training camp because of a troublesome knee situation, will miss a minimum of four games. 'WE BACK': AARON DONALD RETURNS TO THE RAMS AND A DEFENSE NOW LOADED WITH MYLES GARRETT AND OTHERS Garrett will miss games against the New York Giants, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, and Buffalo Bills. He could actually miss more games, depending on his recovery and the success of the upcoming surgery. The good news is the surgery is scheduled as an arthroscopy initially meant to perform a trim rather than a full-blown repair. If that initial expectation based on MRI scans holds, the four-week timetable should be an accurate expectation. RAMS' DISASTER IN AUSTRALIA RAISES THE QUESTION: SHOULD THE TEAM HAVE FOLLOWED THE 49ERS THERE EARLIER? The Rams, the Super Bowl favorite among many pundits before the season began, lost their Week 1 game against the San Francisco 49ers. They did not have Aaron Donald for that game as his ramp-up period after returning from a two-year retirement was not considered complete and the team wanted to be cautious. That caution will remain but the Rams obviously need Donald sooner than later now that they will be without Garrett for a while. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

While Mayfield is 3-0 in Week 1 since arriving in Tampa Bay in 2023, Burrow and the Bengals have often stumbled out of the gate. Cincinnati is 2-4 in openers since Burrow was the top overall pick out of LSU in the 2020 draft.

Mayfield enters today's game with nine touchdowns, no interceptions and a 114.5 passer rating in Week 1 games during his Tampa Bay tenure. He is also mostly free of distractions after signing a $165 million, three-year extension that keeps him with the Bus through 2029.

Mayfield is facing a new-look Bengals defense that features Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen , and Boye Mafe on the defensive line, as well as Bryan Cook at safety.

articles.title: Scott Hanson reveals ‘NFL RedZone’ witching hour secret formula: ‘It is air traffic control’
articles.summary: The NFL technically opened its 2026 season with the Seattle Seahawks beating the New England Patriots and the San Francisco 49ers humiliating the Los Angeles...
articles.body:
The NFL technically opened its 2026 season with the Seattle Seahawks beating the New England Patriots and the San Francisco 49ers humiliating the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively. But true football sickos know that the NFL season does not spiritually start until NFL RedZone monopolizes the first Sunday of the year.

More specifically, the NFL officially reactivates its chokehold on America when RedZone host Scott Hanson guides us through the first " witching hour " of the year. For the uninitiated, the "witching hour" captures the pure chaos of the early-window games finishing simultaneously before giving way to the late window.

'Ladies and gentlemen, eight games going on across the National Football League. Five of them are one-possession games. In Detroit. In New England. In Miami. In Atlanta. And in wherever, Kansas City. articles.title: NFL Picks Against the Spread: Week 1 Games
articles.summary: Which bets do you like the most?
articles.body:
Before the first Sunday of the 2026 regular season kicks off, let's have some fun by taking a look at the lines for the NFL Week 1 games.

My overall record last season was 125-129-1, which was just narrowly behind the BGN community at 126-128-1. Let's see if you can beat me once again.

Here are suggestions when trying to beat the odds.

BUFFALO BILLS (-1.5) at HOUSTON TEXANS : Josh Allen had a 56.4 passer rating against DeMeco Ryans ' defense in 2024. He had a 67.4 passer rating against that unit in 2025. Safe to say that the Texans might have answers for Allen. Give me the home dogs! PICK: Texans +1.5

CHICAGO BEARS (-3) at CAROLINA PANTHERS : The Bears are a regression candidate but they might be able to weather that storm due to Ben Johnson's prowess. Does anyone really have faith in Bryce Young and this Panthers team? Enough to wager on them? PICK: Bears -3

CLEVELAND BROWNS at JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS (-8.5): Betting on Deshaun Watson to come through for me? Yeah, I'll pass. The Browns are prime contenders for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. I don't know if the Jags will be any good … but I could buy them being slept on more than I can buy the Browns doing anything good. PICK: Jaguars -8.5

ATLANTA FALCONS at PITTSBURGH STEELERS (-6.5): Cooper Rush is going to light up this Steelers defense in Pittsburgh ! Now realize how that ridiculous that sounds. PICK: Steelers -6.5

NEW YORK JETS at TENNESSEE TITANS (-1.5): Easier to feel inspired by the Titans' potential for improvement (nowhere to go but up!) than it is by anything the Jets have going on. I'll bet on Cam Ward 's upside before I place any faith in Geno Smith . I could see a Robert Saleh revenge game. PICK: Titans -1.5

NEW ORLEANS SAINTS at DETROIT LIONS (-6.5): The Saints are the trendy sleeper pick but I think the Lions are the NFL's real sleeper. They're going to be much better than they were last season. PICK: Lions -6.5

BALTIMORE RAVENS (-3.5) at INDIANAPOLIS COLTS : The Colts were a flash in a pan for half of the 2025 season. Regular season Lamar Jackson isn't one to bet against. PICK: Ravens -3.5

TAMPA BAY BUCCANEERS at CINCINNATI BENGALS (-3.5): The Bucs would've been friskier had they not paid Baker Mayfield . I'm backing Joe Burrow in this battle. PICK: Bengals -3.5

WASHINGTON COMMANDERS at PHILADELPHIA EAGLES (-5.5): I really just don't like this matchup for the Commanders. Washington has had no answers for Saquon Barkley since he joined the Eagles. The Birds are going to run the ball on this defense. And Philadelphia's pass rush is going to make life difficult for Jayden Daniels . The only hesitation for me here is this line not being larger in the Eagles' favor. But maybe that's just accounting for general Week 1 uncertainty. The Eagles are winning this game. Just a question of by how much. PICK: Eagles -5.5

GREEN BAY PACKERS at MINNESOTA VIKINGS (-1.5): The Packers have some not so good vibes going on. Kyler Murray is hard to trust down the stretch but he could conceivably have some regular season success early on. PICK: Vikings -1.5

MIAMI DOLPHINS at LAS VEGAS RAIDERS (-3): The Dolphins are going to be really bad. The Raiders might also be bad … but I think there's some energy there for them to be more competitive than most would expect. PICK: Raiders -3

ARIZONA CARDINALS at LOS ANGELES CHARGERS (-8.5): Don't know how much I believe in the Bolts, though I am interested to see how the Justin Herbert-Mike McDaniel pairing works out. But it's impossible to believe in the Cardinals. PICK: Chargers -8.5

DALLAS COWBOYS (-3) at NEW YORK GIANTS : As a big benefit of the doubt guy, I can't pick the Giants. Maybe it's a new era for them … but let's see it before we believe it. The Cowboys have owned them for way too long now to predict an upset. I also think Dallas is going to have a good season, unfortunately. PICK: Cowboys -3

DENVER BRONCOS at KANSAS CITY CHIEFS (-2.5): Why should the Chiefs be less than standard three-point favorites? People are sleeping on them and giving the Broncos too much credit. PICK: Chiefs -2.5

articles.title: Former Browns star Myles Garrett headed to IR, getting knee surgery
articles.summary: The former Browns All Pro will miss at least the next four games for the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
Former Browns star Myles Garrett will undergo arthroscopic knee surgery and be placed on injured reserve, according to multiple reports on Sunday, Sept. 13.

Garrett, who was traded from Cleveland to the Los Angeles Rams during the offseason, will miss at least four games. He is eligible to return for the Rams' Week 6 game against the Arizona Cardinals .

The reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year missed most of training camp because of swelling in his knee. He wore a sleeve on his left leg during several practices before the Rams' season opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia.

Garrett said after the loss that his knee was not fully healthy entering the game and called his performance the worst version of himself he had put on the field.

"I've got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be and I've shown that I've been before," Garrett said Friday.

The Rams acquired Garrett in an offseason trade that sent defensive end Jared Verse and three draft picks, including a 2027 first-round pick, to Cleveland .

Garrett set an NFL record with 23 sacks last season for the Browns .

Rams wanted Maxx Crosby before pivoting to Myles Garrett trade with Browns

According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN , the Rams may have passed on acquiring Garrett if their initial idea worked.

Rapoport reported Sunday morning that the Rams initially wanted to trade for Crosby. But the pass rusher who has 69.5 career sacks said he didn't want to be traded by the Las Vegas Raiders .

After that fell apart, the Rams pivoted to Garrett.

The Raiders, meanwhile, traded Crosby to the Baltimore Ravens . It was nixed after Baltimore failed Crosby's physical.

articles.title: Why Colts Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon Stands on Sideline With Headset During NFL Games
articles.summary: Most NFL owners don’t spend games on the sideline.Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon isn’t like most owners. She often can be seen on the sideline...
articles.body:
Most NFL owners don't spend games on the sideline.

Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon isn't like most owners. She often can be seen on the sideline — and sometimes, she has a headset on, too.

Irsay-Gordon took over the role as the principal owner and CEO of the Colts in May 2025 after the death of her father, Jim Irsay.

She co-owns the Colts with her sisters, Casey Fot and Kalen Jackson.

And no, Irsay-Gordon isn't taking over the play-calling operation in Indy. She's simply putting herself more into the action so that she knows what's going on in the organization that she runs.

Why is Colts Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon on the Sideline With a Headset?

Irsay-Gordon decided she'd take an informed approach to ownership of the Colts. She's not trying to influence in-game decisions, but she does want to know what's happening in the franchise that she owns.

None of this is an accident. Irsay-Gordon thinks everything through and has a reason for everything, including this.

"I think one of the things that I learned in going through, even as back as when we hired Chuck Pagano (in 2012), is that sort of accelerated my, 'I need to learn more about this,'" Irsay-Gordon told the Colts' official website in June of 2025 . "'I need to be able to say, is this person full of BS? Do they even know what they're talking about? And I think one of the things that being on the headset has really helped me learn is to the question earlier, it's such a complex organism of football team and how it operates."

Irsay-Gordon sometimes has a play sheet down there, too. If she's going to be able to hear the headset, she wants to be able to connect the dots. It's the only way to get the full picture of the human beings that she's trying to understand.

"You could say, 'Oh, that person ran that route wrong,'" Irsay-Gordon said in that aforementioned story on the Colts' website. "When you learn to find, 'Oh, someone tagged the wrong wide receiver, and it wasn't really the player's fault – it was the person that called it.' I think that's been very valuable, because it also helps us be able to know where do we need to make tweaks, what resources do we need, what do we need to fix. So much of it comes down to just how we operate and how things work and the headsets – I would suggest it for anyone else that has to pay coaches and GMs millions and millions of dollars. It helps you make a less expensive mistake potentially."

Daniel Jones and Shane Steichen both like Irsay-Gordon's leadership of the organization.

"It's neat for sure," Jones told Fox News during the 2025 season . "Just her attention to detail, her interest in how hard she works in understanding every facet of the organization. Obviously, the play on the field, the game plan, the scheme, kind of all that goes into that. She takes a lot of time and makes a lot of effort to get to know that, really, really understand it. I know she's said stuff in the past and how important it is for her to understand all of it as she leads the organization. But, yeah, I think for all of us players it sets a great example seeing the owner on the sideline like that. I think that carries a lot of weight."

Steichen doesn't mind having her on the sideline.

"As far as football, she's around and she understands it," head coach Shane Steichen said in 2025. "When you talk football with her, she gets it. She understands it. She goes over the defensive stuff, the offensive stuff. She's been involved since I've been here from Day One, very hands on and she's been tremendous. I think she's going to do a phenomenal job."

The Colts had a promising start to Irsay-Gordon's first year at the helm before injuries hurt them down the stretch. As the 2026 season gets underway, they'll try to bounce back from that, and Irsay-Gordon will be right there helping lead while also learning along the way.

articles.title: Myles Garrett to reportedly undergo knee surgery, miss at least 4 weeks after struggling in Week 1 loss
articles.summary: Myles Garrett will reportedly have arthroscopic surgery on his knee.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without star pass rusher Myles Garrett for at least the next four weeks due to knee surgery, according to NFL Network.

Garrett, who the team acquired in a blockbuster deal with the Cleveland Browns in the offseason, will reportedly undergo arthroscopic surgery on his knee and will be placed on injured reserve.

The hope is that Garrett will be able to return in four weeks. Garrett previously missed time in training camp with an injury to his left knee, though he did play in the team's Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers .

Garrett wasn't himself in that contest. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year failed to notch a sack or a tackle in the 27-7 loss to the 49ers .

After the contest, Garrett admitted he needed to recover and "get back to the player I know I can be."

The development is a massive blow for the Rams, which gave up Jared Verse and multiple draft picks in exchange for Garrett in the offseason. The star pass rusher was expected to play a massive role in the Rams' push for a Super Bowl this season, and was a big reason former star Aaron Donald came out of retirement to join the Rams for another year.

Garrett still has plenty of time left to be a difference maker for the Rams this season. As long as he doesn't sustain any setbacks, it shouldn't be long before the Rams are fully operational. If they can remain that way late in the season, the team could still live up to its billing as one of the premier contenders to win it all.

articles.title: Saints' scoop-and-score negated after controversial call bails out Lions
articles.summary: Jared Goff's apparent fumble was ruled a forward pass. Here's how one rules expert viewed the tricky play.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints thought they had their first touchdown of the season Sunday in Detroit , coming via a dramatic scoop and score.

Then the referees took it away from them.

With the Lions leading, 7-0, QB Jared Goff dropped back to pass midway through the second quarter, and he was quickly met by Saints pass rusher Chase Young , who knocked the ball loose as Goff went to throw.

The ball caromed backward nearly 15 yards, and it was picked up and run back for an apparent score by Saints DB Jonas Sanker . That would have tied the game at 7-7.

But replay review wiped out the TD. The ruling was an incomplete pass. But how?

Fox officiating expert Mike Pereira tried his best to explain the play — and why the TD was negated.

"[Goff] had started his throwing motion," Pereira said. "Now, throwing motion is bringing the ball up — forget about the hand at this point going forward. Throwing motion starts, hand goes up, then it's hit, ball comes loose. His intent was to throw it forward. And since that motion had already started, that's going to be a forward pass — no matter where it lands."

The Saints are likely going to disagree with that, no matter how the letter of the law is written. Determining Goff's intent on the throw feels suspect, even if a forward pass felt imminent.

Expect to hear more about this call beyond Sunday.

articles.title: Saints defense has touchdown taken away against Lions after Jared Goff fumble is stunningly overturned
articles.summary: Chase Young forced what looked like a Jared Goff fumble, but officials ruled it an incomplete pass, wiping a New Orleans Saints defensive touchdown.
articles.body: The New Orleans Saints scored a routine defensive touchdown against the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon. Or so they thought, or so everyone thought. With the Lions on top 7-0 early in the second quarter, New Orleans defensive end Chase Young beat his man on the edge and forced what looked to be a routine fumble out of Detroit quarterback Jared Goff. It appeared to be a straightforward fumble given that the ball traveled backward, and Goff's arm did not look to be moving forward. Saints safety Jonas Sanker ultimately picked up the football and carried it into the end zone untouched to get New Orleans on the scoreboard, but only for a brief moment. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! After reviewing the play, officials determined that Goff had started his throwing motion, and given that the quarterback's intent was to throw the football forward, it was ruled an incomplete pass. ZAC TAYLOR ADMITS BREAKING NFL CHALLENGE FLAG RULE FOR 8 YEARS AS LEAGUE MAKES CHANGE The football didn't actually travel forward, but Goff's intention overrules the fact that the ball traveled backward, apparently. "He had started his throwing motion," Mike Pereira, NFL rules analyst for Fox Sports, explained on the broadcast. "Now, throwing motion is bringing the ball up; forget about the hand at this point going forward. Throwing motion starts, hand going up, then he's hit, ball comes loose, his intent was to throw it forward. Since that motion had already started, that's going to be an incomplete pass, no matter where it lands." While taking intent into consideration feels like a gray area, especially during a bang-bang play, the explanation that it doesn't matter where the football actually lands makes the rule that much more confusing. articles.title: Josiah Trotter, Jeremiah Trotter's son, has sack, pick 6 in historic NFL debut
articles.summary: Trotter's father and brother played in the NFL before him. One game into his career, he's already making a name for himself.
articles.body:
Josiah Trotter comes from strong NFL pedigree. He put it on full display in his NFL debut.

A rookie linebacker for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , Trotter is the son of former Philadelphia Eagles All-Pro Jeremiah Trotter. After a standout college career with Missouri and West Virginia, Trotter was a second-round selection by the Bucs in April's NFL Draft.

His first NFL game on Sunday was one to remember. Early in the third quarter of Sunday's game against the Bengals , Trotter came up with a sack of Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow .

The third-down ended Cincinnati's drive and forced the Bengals to settle for a field goal.

On Cincinnati's next possession, Trotter came up even bigger. This time Burrow threw a pass in the flat on third-and-5 targeting Andrei Iosivas . Trotter was in coverage and jumped the route.

He intercepted the ball in stride and ran untouched down the left sideline for a pick 6.

The touchdown cut Cincinnati's lead to 27-20 late in the third quarter and made a once 21-3 game competitive. And, per the Associated Press , Trotter is the first player since sacks became an official stat in 1982 to record a sack and a pick 6 in his NFL debut.

Unfortunately for the Bucs, the effort didn't help them to victory in a 33-27 Bengals win .

Trotter's father, Jeremiah, had a standout 11-season NFL career playing for Philadelphia, Washington and Tampa Bay . He made four Pro Bowls and was twice named All-Pro. His brother, Jeremiah Trotter Jr., is a third-year pro playing for the Eagles.

Now Josiah's in the NFL looking to make a name for himself with the Bucs. So far so good in a remarkable NFL debut.

articles.title: Zay Flowers ruled out in Week 1 with hamstring injury after dominant first half
articles.summary: Zay Flowers was already having a career day when he went down with an injury.
articles.body:
It's early, but Baltimore Ravens wideout Zay Flowers looked like he had taken a major step forward early in Week 1. But a dominant first half ended on a sour note, as Flowers left the game against the Indianapolis Colts due to a hamstring injury.

He was initially deemed questionable to return, but was later downgraded to out.

The injury came at an unfortunate time for Flowers, who was already having a career day before half time. When he left the contest, Flowers had five catches for a career-high 150 yards.

One of those catches was a 54-yard touchdown strike, in which he weaved his way through the Colts' defense for the score.

Just prior to halftime, Flowers limped on the sideline, per ESPN. He dealt with a hamstring injury throughout training camp, causing him to miss multiple weeks. Flowers, however, was able to return in time to practice in full ahead of Week 1.

After halftime, Flowers was spotted walking slowly on the sideline. When the Ravens took the field, he was not included in the team's first three-receiver set of the second half.

Turns out, that was all the Ravens had for the rest of Week 1, as rookie Ja'Kobi Lane was ruled out with a wrist injury . Once Flowers was also ruled out, the Ravens were limited to Rashod Bateman , Chris Moore and LaJohntay Wester at receiver the rest of the contest.

Big things are expected from Flowers after he signed a four-year, $140 million extension in August. He's gained over 1,000 receiving yards in each of the past two seasons.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson's first-possession interception sets tone for Jaguars rout of Browns
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson heard boos from the home crowd in his first preseason game with the Cleveland Browns. He's on track to hear more when he makes his regular-sea...
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson heard boos from the home crowd in his first preseason home game last month with the Cleveland Browns .

He's on track to hear more when he makes his regular-season home debut — that is if he still has his job as Cleveland's starting quarterback.

Watson threw an interception on Cleveland's first drive of the the season Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars . The turnover sparked a 34-10 Jaguars rout and the start of what looks like another difficult season in Cleveland.

While Trevor Lawrence looked ready to pick back up where he left off from a standout 2025 campaign in a nearly perfect four-touchdown game, Watson's effort left much to be desired.

Watson finished his day completing 16-of-22 passes for 205 yards with 1 touchdown, 1 interception, 1 fumble and 5 sacks taken. His and Cleveland's lone touchdown arrived in the final two minutes of a game that had long been lost. His interception to start the game set the tone for what was coming.

Watson's mistake sparks Jacksonville rout

With 12:17 remaining in the first quarter, the Browns faced second-and-5 from the Jacksonville 28-yard line. They'd driven 32 yards and were in good shape to secure at least a field goal on the opening drive of the game.

Watson looked downfield to receiver Jerry Jeudy , who was on a curl route near the 10-yard line. Instead, he found Jaguars linebacker Foyesade Oluokun , who intercepted the pass and returned it to the Jacksonville 41.

Oluokun was lurking in underneath coverage, and Watson didn't appear to see him. He threw the ball directly to the Jaguars linebacker.

Eight plays later, Trevor Lawrence found Parker Washington for a touchdown, and the Jaguars took an early 7-0 lead.

The pass was Watson's third of the season and his third since 2024. Watson's career was derailed that season by a combination of injury and poor play, and he hadn't played an NFL snap since until Sunday.

Two possessions later and with the Jaguars holding a 14-0 lead, Watson fumbled while being sacked. The Browns recovered the ball, but the play exacerbated a poor start for the veteran quarterback.

By halftime, the Jaguars were rolling to a 24-0 lead, and concerns about another poor season in Cleveland were amped up to full volume. Lawrence had three touchdown passes against a hapless Browns defense, and Jacksonville dominated the ball.

Cleveland's best shot at scoring on a no-huddle drive at the end of the half was derailed by a pair of holding penalties that pushed them back from the verge of field-goal range.

As for Watson, he completed 8-of-12 passes in the first half for 75 yards with 1 interception, 1 fumble and 2 sacks taken, and the game was virtually lost.

Late TD pads stats with no impact on game

There was little reason for encouragement in Cleveland after halftime. Lawrence marched the Jaguars to an opening-drive touchdown in the third quarter to extend the lead to 31-0. He finished his day completing 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards with four touchdowns and no turnovers.

The Browns responded with a drive inside the 5-yard line on their first possession of the half. But a delay-of-game penalty on third-and-2 at the 3 stunted the drive, and the Browns settled for a field goal just to get on the board.

Cleveland's last drive and late touchdown padded Watson's stat line. But there was little from Watson's effort Sunday to give Cleveland hope for a career resurgence since he won the starting job.

Watson won the job in training camp over second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders , who demonstrated little in his rookie campaign that he was capable of playing as an NFL starter. It's been rough going for Watson since.

Head coach Todd Monken insinuated that Watson's hold on the job was tenuous, noting that he believed Watson gave Cleveland the best chance in a game "to start the season on the road."

"[I] took in the whole body of work over the course of offseason to training camp to games, the joint practice and ultimately felt like, to start the season on the road, Deshaun gave us the best chance to move the ball and score points," Monken said in August. "That's really what it's about."

Watson, meanwhile, is not a popular man in Cleveland.

Watson, who joined the Browns in 2022 on the heels of a scandal in which he was accused of sexual misconduct by 27 women , was greeted with boos by Cleveland fans in the preseason. He responded to the boos by chastising Browns fans to reporters.

Sunday's game was in Jacksonville, or he likely would have heard more boos before halftime. If Watson remains the starter in Week 3 for Cleveland's home debut against the Carolina Panthers on Sept. 27, there's a decent chance more boos will await him.

articles.title: Ravens start fast and pound Colts, 41-23, in Jesse Minter’s debut
articles.summary: INDIANAPOLIS — Explosive was the word of the summer among Baltimore Ravens players and coaches. There was mystery about how exactly it would manifest once th...
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — Explosive was the word of the summer among Baltimore Ravens players and coaches. There was mystery about how exactly it would manifest once they got to the regular season.

On Baltimore's first offensive play of the game, Lamar Jackson faked a handoff to Derrick Henry , rolled back to his left and found Zay Flowers streaking across the field. The Pro Bowl receiver made the catch near the sideline, hit the brakes, spun back toward the middle and raced for what ended up being a 49-yard completion to the Indianapolis 2-yard line to set up a touchdown.

A quarter later and on a second-and-9 from his own 41 with a blitz bearing down on Jackson, the quarterback quick-fired a short pass to Flowers in a soft spot in the defense. Flowers hit the gas, slicing his way through the Colts ' defense for a 54-yard touchdown.

That gave the Ravens all the cushion they needed en route to a 41-23 victory in which Baltimore also forced two turnovers in coach Jesse Minter's debut.

Flowers finished with a career-high 150 yards on five receptions, but the victory was soured by the franchise receiver suffering a hamstring injury in the second quarter that knocked him out of the game. Baltimore also lost promising rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane to a wrist injury after he was ruled out early in the third.

The same left hamstring that sidelined Flowers for almost two full weeks leading up to Week 1 plagued him again Sunday. He came up grabbing his leg after a 12-yard catch at the 5:57 mark of the second and one play before a 32-yard touchdown run by Henry.

With Flowers and Lane out, Baltimore was perilously thin at the position with Rashod Bateman , LaJohntay Wester and Chris Moore , who was elevated from the practice squad for the game, their only other available receivers, and the offense stalled.

Baltimore committed 10 penalties for 86 yards, with the offense being the primary culprit.

Most costly was a holding penalty on center Jovaughn Gwyn — who was making his first career start — that took a 4-yard touchdown pass to Lane early in the second quarter off the board. A holding penalty on rookie guard Vega Ioane also wiped out a first-down completion to Bateman, and an illegal shift early in the third did the same for a first-down pass to Mark Andrews .

Still, the Ravens had enough firepower on both sides of the ball to outmaneuver the Colts.

Linebacker Roquan Smith intercepted Daniel Jones (19 of 31 passing, 166 yards) at the Colts' 32-yard line midway through the first quarter to help set up Baltimore's second touchdown of the game, a 4-yard score from Henry (24 carries, 144 yards). Then, Marlon Humphrey stripped running back Jonathan Taylor and recovered the fumble to set up Henry's eventual 32-yard score.

That gave Baltimore a 28-6 lead before a strip-sack of Jackson set the Colts up at the Ravens' 15 and a Taylor touchdown from 3 yards out to cut the deficit to 28-13.

Both teams then traded field goals, which included struggling Ravens kicker Tyler Loop converting a career-long 57-yarder as time ran out in the second quarter.

While the Ravens' offense struggled to move the ball in the second half, Jackson did connect with Moore for a 53-yard strike on third-and-5 to start the fourth quarter. Three plays later, Henry scored again, this time from three yards.

Jackson also provided perhaps the game's most spectacular play.

With the Colts' Arden Key and DeForest Buckner converging on the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player on a third-and-16 from the Colts' 37 for an apparent sack midway through the opening quarter, Jackson did his best Houdini impression.

He ducked, then slipped through the two defenders like a water balloon on a hot day and raced downfield for a first down.

Earlier this summer, Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton said Jackson looked like he'd gotten faster in what is his ninth NFL season.

It wasn't always pretty, but the Ravens got off to the flying start they were hoping for.

articles.title: Buccaneers Week 1 Top Performers at Cincinnati Bengals
articles.summary: Well, it’s only Week 1.
articles.body:
The Buccaneers came into 2026 looking to distance themselves from their disaster 2025 campaign…and proceeded to showcase many of the same issues that plagued them last year.

Baker Mayfield playing recklessly, the defense allowing way too many freebies, and general communication issues plagued the Bucs from start to finish as they floundered to a 33-27 defeat in Cincinnati. Four turnovers (all fumbles, three from Mayfield) led to 24 of Cincinnati's 33 points.

There were some bright spots across the roster, but there needs to be massive amounts of cleanup when the Bucs stage their home-opener next week against the Cleveland Browns .

Offensive Top Performer: RB Bucky Irving

The biggest sigh of relief on the offensive side might've been how good Bucky Irving looked — minus an early lost fumble. After suffering through serious knee and shoulder injuries last season, Irving looked explosive and decisive in new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson's new wide zone-based scheme.

Irving commanded the snap load, out-touching newcomer Kenny Gainwell 15 to 6. Irving rushed 8 times for 45 yards and a touchdown and added 7 catches for 48 yards.

If he can remain the dangerous dual-threat weapon he established himself as in 2024, the entire offensive process should stabilize.

When Mayfield was functioning properly in the dropback passing game, Chris Godwin and Emeka Egbuka both created some moments. Godwin looked like he wanted to hunt defensive backs, leaning into contact and even administering a vicious stiff arm at one point en route to 4 catches for 40 yards. Egbuka broke a few chunk receptions, snagging 5 catches for 63 yards.

Overall, Robinson called a good game that got sabotaged by turnovers. The process needs tweaking but yards and scores were there to be had.

Defensive Top Performer: LB Josiah Trotter

The temptation to give a Week 1 "nobody" here was strong through nearly 3 quarters, but luckily a positive development brewed in the form rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter.

Trotter, who's only 21, went through some characteristic debut ups and downs in the first half, exasperated by his running mate Alex Anzalone 's inability to do literally anything at a competent level. The second half told a much different tale, as Trotter looked more confident and trusting of his instincts, which paid off in a big way in the form of a sack ( Tampa 's only one of the game) and a 38-yard pick-six. The list of NFL players who have gotten a sack and a pick-six in their debut: Josiah Trotter.

It's only Week 1, but the Bucs, who were already very high on Trotter, will be feeling good about him after Sunday.

There's not much else to comment on here. The defense still hemorrhaged yards in the middle of the field, it still suffered from miscommunications, and there were still issues with missed tackles. Basically nothing changed, and that is extremely concerning.

If they make whatever schmuck the Browns trot out next week look competent, the seat is going to be red hot for Todd Bowles early.

Special Teams Top Performer: K Chase McLaughlin

Chase McLaughlin needs his extension, as he remains one of the league's elite kickers.

He nailed both his field goal attempts to keep the Bucs somewhat in it, one being from 51 yards out.

On an overall note, the coverage and return units looked solid. After how awful last season was, that will be a welcome relief. The Bucs allowed a long kick return of just 26 yards. That said, both teams punted a grand total of once, so we didn't see the punt side of things get put to work.

articles.title: Cam Ward, Titans struggle mightily in Week 1 loss to Jets
articles.summary: Save for one good touchdown drive in garbage time, Ward started his second NFL season with a game to forget.
articles.body:
Cam Ward did not get his second NFL season off to a good start. The Tennessee Titans quarterback had a tough showing in a 23-10 Week 1 loss to the New York Jets , throwing poorly save for one drive towards the end of the game.

Ward's stats for the game were pretty rough, with the 24-year-old throwing 19-of-32 for 140 yards and one touchdown.

That touchdown, Ward's only shining moment in the matchup, came off a strong drive in the final minutes of the game. Ward pulled the Titans 65 yards down the field in nine plays and just under two-and-a-half minutes for the garbage time score.

The touchdown drive was the only reason that Ward broke 100 passing yards and passed 50% on passing completion; if you remove it, Ward's stats are even more bleak.

Among the Tennessee offense, it wasn't just Ward that struggled: The Titans only put up 195 total yards, including just 68 on the ground, and held almost half as much possession time as the Jets. Ward was also sacked three times in the matchup, indicating problems in the offensive line; and the Tennessee defense at one point seemed to have 13 players on the field, but still couldn't hold off a touchdown from Breece Hall .

But the performance from Ward, hailed as the future of the franchise, was the most worrying. More than just missing his throws, the young QB often just looked lost on the field.

And again, this was a resounding loss to a pretty mediocre Jets team. Tennessee looked toothless against a New York team that was still making plenty of its characteristic mistakes — like losing nearly 50 yards on penalties, or getting the ball on a recovered fumble off a kickoff and then missing a field goal.

While it's still a little too early in the season to panic, it's a bad omen for the kind of season that that Titans might be having. Expectations for the team were already low , but Ward's struggles indicate that the team's future — already in need of so many structural changes — might also need a new quarterback to guide them.

The Jets, meanwhile, are already starting the season with a lot more positives. New York scored on its very first drive of the game, with Kenyon Sadiq running into the corner of the end zone; they picked up 367 total yards and looked like a solidly competent offense to start the year.

The one things that the Jets didn't get was an interception. New York didn't record a pick during the entire 2025 season, and is hoping to break that streak sooner rather than later.

articles.title: Watch: Kyler Murray lobs up interception on first pass attempt as a Viking
articles.summary: That's not exactly how Murray wanted his Vikings tenure to begin.
articles.body:
Kyler Murray probably had something else in mind when thinking about what his first pass in a Vikings uniform would look like.

On the second play from scrimmage in Sunday's season opener against the Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium, Murray had an unblocked blitzer bearing down on him in an empty, five-wide set. He lofted a deep ball for Jauan Jennings that was easily picked off by Green Bay cornerback Keisean Nixon .

Vikings right guard Will Fries appeared to mess up his assignment on the play — and wound up on his back in the process.

That's not quite the kind of first impression Murray was hoping to make in front of his new home crowd. The Vikings' defense mostly held up on the ensuing possession, but the Packers converted a 59-yard field goal to take an early 3-0 lead.

It's the 61st career interception in 88 NFL games for Murray, who has never thrown more than 12 picks in a season. The good news is that there's a lot of game left for him to shake off that poor start.

articles.title: Panthers 37 Bears 59: A shootout to open the season
articles.summary: The offense looked very good, but the defense was about as bad as we’ve ever seen it as the Carolina Panthers dropped their season opener to the Chicago Bear...
articles.body:
The offense looked very good, but the defense was about as bad as we've ever seen it as the Carolina Panthers dropped their season opener to the Chicago Bears , 59-37.

The Bears got the ball first, and on the first play D'Andre Swift ripped right through the middle of the defense for a big gain. However, it was called back for a holding penalty. Two plays later, two offseason acquisitions made their first impacts. Bobby Okereke punched the ball out from Luther Burden III , and rookie Will Lee IV recovered it.

Bryce Young hit Tommy Tremble across the middle to get the drive started. A few plays later he found Jalen Coker deep down the right sideline, who made a spectacular toe tapping catch inside the five. The Panthers scored a couple plays later on a pass to Darren Waller , but he was called for a questionable pass interference. No matter. A couple plays later, Young eluded pressure and found Chuba Hubbard wide open for a touchdown.

The Bears responded. D'Andre Swift picked up some more big chunks that weren't called back. Caleb Williams found space with some scrambles as well. The last of those came deep in Panthers territory, and he scampered down the right sideline for a game tying touchdown.

The Panthers got good field position after the kickoff missed the landing zone, but they didn't do anything with it. Xavier Legette dropped a bubble screen then Young was sacked on third down. A short punt gave the Bears their own good field position. A couple plays into the drive Lee let Rome Odinze run free and was very lackadaisical trying to recover ground. He got mossed at the catch point, setting up 1st and goal. Two plays later, Swift punched in the Bears second touchdown. The first quarter ended with the Panthers going three and out for the second straight drive.

A penalty on the punt gave the Bears the ball in Panthers territory to start their next drive. Kyle Monangai was wide open on a checkdown to big up a big gain. On the next play, Caleb Williams threw a dime to Cole Kmet , who pulled the ball in for the Bears' third touchdown in as many possessions.

The Panthers answered quickly. Young found Coker across the middle for a nice gain. After a short run for Hubbard, Young went deep for Coker again, and he reeled it in behind the defense for a 51 yard touchdown.

The defense finally pulled their weight. They limited the Bears offense to a couple of short gains and brought up 4th and inches. The Bears went for it despite being on their own 20. The defense bowed up and stuffed the sneak. Tetairoa McMillan got his first catch of the season on the ensuing drive to take the offense inside the 10. After an exchange of penalties, Young bobbed and weaved on a scramble and weathered a big hit to tie the game up at 21.

The defense once again forced a three and out after Trevis Gipson made a great backside tackle against his former team. This time the Bears punted, and Jimmy Horn Jr. completely whiffed on the punt and muffed it back to Chicago. The defense held up though and forced a field goal.

Young found Jonathon Brooks up the sideline on a scramble drill for a 50 yard gain. That got the Panthers into field goal range, and that's what they had to settle for. Ryan Fitzgerald knocked through the 44 yarder.

Jaelan Phillips sacked Caleb Williams on the first play of the two minute drive, but Williams was able to make a highlight throw on 3rd and long to keep the drive alive. A few plays later, Williams broke contain and again took off down a wide open left sideline for a 29 yard touchdown.

The Panthers tried to force the issue in the last 22 seconds. Young got picked off trying to make a play, but it was an inconsequential interception with just five seconds left.

The Panthers got the ball first coming out of the half and unceremoniously went three and out. The Bears did the same thanks to a sack by Princely Umanmielen . Jimmy Horn Jr. almost fumbled again but was fortunately down before the ball came out.

Chuba Hubbard was a bit more assertive running the ball and tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble had some nice catches to move the offense down the field with haste. They ended up on the doorstep of the goal line, and Hubbard was able to punch in his second touchdown of the game.

The Bears marched down the field with a handful of modest games. The defense forced the Bears into a 2nd and 20 after a run stuff and a holding penalty, but Derrick Brown was called for roughing the passer to gift the Bears a first down at the 11 yard line. Three handoffs to D'Andre Swift ended with the Bears in the end zone once again.

Another illegal kick gave the Panthers good field position, and another in breaker to Jalen Coker crossed midfield. The Panthers found themselves in a 4th and short and left the offense on the field, but Young overthrew McMillan on a corner route. On the first play after the turnover, Kyle Monangai ran right through the middle of the defense for a 61 yard touchdown.

Young found McMillan wide open across the middle of the field for a huge gain, but he had the ball punched out when he got tackled.

The defense got the Bears into a couple of third downs but they kept leaving large gaps in coverage and let the Bears pick up easy first downs. Caleb Williams ran the ball all the way down to the goal line. Bobby Brown tipped a pass to himself and picked it off, but it was called back because Derrick Brown was lined up in the neutral zone. A couple plays later, Williams found Johdae Walker uncovered in the end zone for a knockout punch touchdown.

Young shoveled a ball to Hubbard under pressure for a 29 yard gain. He then completed back to back passes for McMillan for another 33 to get inside the five. He found Mitchell Evans for a touchdown, but it was called back for a pick by Jalen Coker. Coker made amends a couple plays later by shedding a tackle and waltzing in for a touchdown. The extra point was blocked just because this game was nuts.

In a fitting way to close the game, the Panthers defense had the Bears in a 3rd and 2 needing a stop for one last desperation attempt to get back into the game, but Trevis Gipson jumped offsides on the hard count and gave up the first down. Two plays later, D'Andre Swift ripped right through the middle of the defense once again for yet another touchdown.

On one hand, the offense was encouraging. Bryce Young pushed the ball down the field and was aggressive fitting the ball into windows. It was one of the better games he's played in his career, and it was by far the best he's played in a season opener.

On the other hand, the defense was as bad as we've seen it. The Bears offense won what felt like 80% of the plays. They were gashed in the run game, couldn't get Caleb Williams on the ground, and left huge openings for receivers. Compounding the problems by the defense were self inflicted mistakes by players that the Panthers are counting on. Derrick Brown committed two penalties in the red zone that gave the Bears new life after a rare defensive win and Tetairoa McMillan fumbled away a must score possession. Those have to be cleaned up, and it goes without saying that the defense has to figure something out if this team is going to compete for anything. You're not going to win any games giving up 300 yards on the ground.

The Panthers will try to tighten things up as they get ready for their first divisional game next week against the Faclons.

Pittsburgh Steelers ' 2024 first-round offensive tackle Troy Fautanu has dealt with multiple knee injuries in his three-year NFL career. At first glance, it appeared Fautanu picked up another serious setback in the Week 1 season opener against the Atlanta Falcons , but the Steelers undoubtedly dodged a bullet.

Following an 17-yard rush in the fourth quarter by Warren, in which he was pushed forward by multiple Steelers teammates, Fautanu went down due to a possible knee injury, heading to the sideline with trainers as fans waited with bated breath. Luckily for the Steelers, there was no blue tent trip for the young offensive tackle, as Fautanu retook the field soon after.

While Fautanu was down, Max Iheanachor made his NFL debut at right tackle while Dylan Cook moved over to the left side.

Fautanu, drafted by the Steelers in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft, suffered a sprained MCL in his right knee in August of his rookie season, and then a season-ending dislocated knee injury one month later.

Mike McCarthy may provide more details on Fautanu's condition during the post-game press conference, but the Steelers likely caught a huge break in this win.
