articles.title: Bills-Texans looked like an AFC Championship preview in Week 1, and Buffalo was a step ahead
articles.summary: Texans-Bills was billed as a potential AFC Championship Game. It lived up to the hype
articles.body:
The game was billed as a potential AFC Championship Game preview.

Given how it played out, sign us up for a rematch sometime in January.

The Houston Texans hosted the Buffalo Bills in the early slate of the first full Sunday of the 2026 NFL season, and these two playoff hopefuls threw haymaker after haymaker in an instant classic, won by the Bills by a final score of 36-31

But the score alone does not do this game justice.

The teams combined for a stunning 45 points in the first half alone, as the Bills racked up 224 total yards and 12 first downs in the first 30 minutes, all of that coming against one of the league's top defenses. Not to be outdone, C.J. Stroud and the Houston offense tallied 215 total yards and 16 first downs of their own, as the Bills took a 24-21 lead into the halftime break.

However, this game was just getting started.

That halftime break seemed to favor the defenses, as both offenses stalled on their respective drives to open the second half.

Eventually a field goal from Tyler Bass staked Buffalo to a 27-21 lead, and the pressure was back on Stroud and the Texans offense to respond.

They did, on a lengthy drive that needed a pair of fourth-down conversions. The first came on a tough run from David Montgomery , with Houston facing 4th-and-1 in their own territory. The second came on a 4th-and-inches play in Bills' territory, as this time it was Woody Marks converting the hard yards inside to move the chains.

That Marks run was the final play of the third quarter, and the teams flipped the field to open the final frame with Houston facing a 1st-and-10 at the Buffalo 19-yard line. After a completion and a short run, Stroud gave the Texans the lead, connecting with Montgomery on this short touchdown pass:

It was the fifth lead change of the day.

Not when the quarterback on the other side of the field is Allen, who can flip the field with a flick of the wrist, as he did here:

Ultimately, Buffalo's ensuing drive stalled and Bass was called upon to try a 33-yard field goal. The Bills kicker split the uprights to make it a 30-28 game, the sixth lead change of the afternoon.

The seventh lead change was right around the corner, as Ka'imi Fairbairn drilled a 58-yard field goal to stake the Texans to a 31-30 lead with under seven minutes to go. The Texans defense, despite giving up 30 points to that moment in the game, was in position to close out the contest.

They forced a quick three-and-out, living up to their own hype and giving Stroud and the offense a chance to extend Houston's lead. But Buffalo's defense forced a three-and-out of their own, giving Allen a chance to orchestrate another lead change.

That was, as my high school literature teacher would love to remind me, a bit of foreshadowing.

The Bills and their quarterback would need to travel nearly the length of the field, after a punt from Kai Kroeger of the Texans pinned Buffalo inside their own 5-yard line. But a big run from James Cook and a pair of completions moved the Bills out to their own 32-yard line by the two-minute warning.

Up in the booth, Ross Tucker was noting that the game's biggest play had yet to materialize. What would this game's closing chapter deliver?

That closing chapter began with another connection between Allen and Dalton Kincaid , as the two connected on a 35-yard pass play to get the Bills into Houston territory, and within striking distance for Bass:

Allen, under pressure in the pocket, lofted a throw in the direction of Joshua Palmer in the end zone. It was off target, and fell into the lap of Texans defender Kamari Lassiter . It would have been a game-ending interception.

He dropped it, giving Allen a second life.

The Buffalo quarterback made the most of it:

Given that second life, Allen threads the needle to Palmer on a post route, and the Bills are in the end zone, and back in the lead.

Joe Brady kept the offense on the field to try a two-point conversion, to try and make it a seven-point advantage. But Allen was forced to throw the ball out of the end zone under pressure, and the Bills settled for a 36-31 lead.

Still, there was time for Stroud and the Texans.

A pair of completions to Dalton Schultz moved the Texans into Buffalo territory, and with Houston still having a pair of timeouts remaining, the full field was open to the Houston passer. A defensive penalty moved the ball to the Buffalo 34-yard line, and the Texans still had both timeouts at their disposal.

A false start from Trent Brown backed Houston up five, setting up a 1st-and-15. An incompletion and a 12-yard completion to Nico Collins put the Texans into a 3rd-and-3 situation, still with one timeout in their hands.

Stroud then hit Jaylin Noel along the sideline for a big gain, taking advantage of a bust in the coverage. The completion moved Houston to within the 10-yard line, with 25 seconds remaining.

Buffalo then dropped Stroud for a sack, forcing the Texans to burn their final time out. It was Deone Walker , getting home with a swim move on the inside, to bring down the Houston quarterback.

Stroud then tried to hit Collins along the sideline, and that pass fell incomplete, setting up a 3rd-and-goal situation with just 16 seconds remaining. Without that final timeout, things were getting tougher for Houseon.

Stroud was sacked again, coughed up the football, and the Bills recovered:

Ultimately, it was the Bills defense that made the biggest play of the game. And it was Greg Rousseau , a first-round pick back in 2021, who got home on the strip sack to ice the game.

It was a statement win for Brady in his head-coaching debut, but it was his defense that made the biggest statement. While the Texans defense generated the bulk of the headlines this offseason, given what Houston had done last year and the addition of safety Reed Blankenship and several depth pieces including Jadeveon Clowney , on this afternoon it was Buffalo's unit that stood tallest in the game's biggest moment.

But given how both teams looked, a rematch of this meeting in January certainly feels like a possibility.

articles.title: Bills cracked Texans' dominant defense. Takeaways from wild AFC tilt
articles.summary: The Bills and Texans combined for 67 points and eight lead changes. Here are the key takeaways from Buffalo's wild win.
articles.body:
Maybe Houston Texans defensive end Will Anderson Jr. wasn't being hyperbolic after all.

The prolific pass rusher and 2025 runner-up for NFL Defensive Player of the Year set up his team's Week 1 showdown against the Buffalo Bills by saying it was an "AFC Championship matchup." That unquestionably was lofty framing for two franchises that have combined for one appearance in the game in the last five years.

Sunday's 36-31 win by the Bills, however, served as a reminder of just how formidable both Buffalo and Houston can be when at peak form. The back-and-forth affair featured eight lead changes and never seemed in hand until the very end.

Each team leaves the tilt with additional reason to believe a breakthrough could be ahead, as well as several things to work on in order to reach the conference title game stage.

Here are the key takeaways from the matchup:

A first look at the new Highmark Stadium, home of the Buffalo Bills, Josh Allen

Last November, Anderson and Danielle Hunter combined for 4 ½ of the eight sacks on Josh Allen that powered the Texans' 23-19 win over the Bills. On Sunday, the league's best edge-rushing duo didn't make much of a dent until late in the fourth quarter. Anderson had just a half-sack while Hunter logged none against a front that afforded Allen plenty of time to work deep.

Offseason acquisition DJ Moore did plenty to help unlock that vertical game, with the highlight coming when he hauled in a dart down the right sideline from Allen that he then took in for a 43-yard score. He finished with five catches for 100 yards in a stellar debut for his third pro team. His presence helped compensate for a ground game that, outside of Allen's 21-yard scramble for a touchdown, couldn't find its form of last year.

The early struggles were a foreign experience for Houston. The defense had not surrendered 24 points in a half since Week 2 of 2023 – the second game of DeMeco Ryans ' tenure.

The Texans seemed to find their footing a bit more after halftime, allowing just two field goals until the final two minutes. But cornerback Kamari Lassiter couldn't secure a deep heave for a potentially game-sealing interception, and he was burned on the ensuing play by Joshua Palmer for the winning 34-yard scoring strike.

Even after Houston gave up two picks in a package to acquire David Montgomery, some wondered whether the veteran running back might end up stuck in a backfield timeshare with Woody Marks . On Sunday, the Texans reinforced just how central Montgomery is to their offensive plans.

The powerful runner notched three total touchdowns – two rushing, one receiving – and set the tone for a methodical offense with his 79 total yards on 23 touches. Montgomery also showed nice burst when he found the hole and then outraced the defense for an 18-yard score.

His output might not seem scintillating, but it helped set the tone for a unit that might be at its best playing an efficient form of keep-away. Houston converted seven of 16 third downs and held onto the ball for nearly 13 minutes more than Buffalo. And after ranking 29th in red-zone efficiency in 2025, the Texans found the end zone on four of five trips there against the Bills.

Bills' work-in-progress D eventually rattles C.J. Stroud late

New coordinator Jim Leonhard acknowledged before the season that the extensive changes he was instituting would necessitate an acclimation period for Buffalo's defense. Sunday provided a peek at just how steep that learning curve might be.

Facing a Texans team with a dearth of pass-catching weapons and an offensive front that remains under construction, the Bills surrendered 386 yards and 21 first downs. But while C.J. Stroud seldom faced pressure throughout the day, Buffalo generated two of its three sacks to mount a game-clinching stand.

After a coverage breakdown allowed the Texans to reach Buffalo's 9-yard line with 25 seconds remaining, 331-pound defensive tackle Deone Walker shook right guard Ed Ingram en route to a sack of Stroud. Two plays later, Greg Rousseau pushed around the edge to get his hands on Stroud and force a fumble, which was recovered by Terrel Bernard .

The Bills' performance suggested their defense might only go as far as the hot-and-cold pass rush takes it. There won't be much time to figure things out on the fly, either, as the home opener against the explosive Detroit Lions looms on Thursday.

articles.title: T.J. Watt’s highlight-reel pick-six vaults Steelers to Week 1 win
articles.summary: T.J. Watt's pick-six paved the way for the Pittsburgh Steelers' 20-13 win on Sunday.
articles.body:
It was the T.J. Watt show for the Pittsburgh Steelers against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday.

He was everywhere on defense, finishing with four total tackles, two sacks, and an interception returned for a touchdown.

His pick-six was especially absurd and helped the Steelers defeat the Atlanta Falcons 20-13. Early in the fourth quarter, with the Steelers up 13-10, Watt jumped and intercepted a Cooper Rush pass. He fell to the ground but wasn't touched, then got up and ran into the end zone for a touchdown.

It's a special play made by a special player. It's what Watt can do as a gamebreaker.

Per ESPN Insights , Watt joins Julius Peppers as the only two players with 100 sacks and 10 interceptions since sacks became an official stat in 1982. He's been one of the best pass rushers in the NFL since he came into the league in 2017, and that's not changing anytime soon.

T.J. Watt helps Mike McCarthy get his first win

Sunday's win was Mike McCarthy's first win as head coach of the Steelers. He was hired to replace Mike Tomlin during the offseason after Tomlin stepped down.

Watt will try to help the Steelers get off to a 2-0 start next Sunday when they travel to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots . They'll play a Patriots team that will be without star wideout A.J. Brown after he sprained his ankle on Wednesday.

articles.title: Panthers, Bears make NFL history with wild Week 1 shootout
articles.summary: The Panthers and Bears put on the highest-scoring Week 1 matchup in NFL history on Sunday.
articles.body:
If you like offense, today's regular-season opener for the Carolina Panthers offered all you could possibly eat . . . and then some.

The reigning NFC South champions and the reigning NFC North champions combined for a whopping 96 points, the most ever for a Week 1 matchup in NFL history. But unfortunately for Carolina, it was the Chicago Bears who came out on top— 59-37 .

The Panthers took an early lead after a turnover by the Bears, but Chicago's offense proved too potent even for Carolina's supposedly much-improved defense.

Quarterback Caleb Williams threw for 269 yards and two touchdowns, but it was the Bears' run game that really did the damage. In a throwback to their record-worst run defense in 2024, the Panthers allowed the Bears to record 291 yards on the ground plus a painful six rushing touchdowns—two of them coming from Williams on scrambles.

The Panthers' offense was plenty explosive themselves, including a brilliant game from their own No. 1 overall pick, Bryce Young . He threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns, two of them going to wide receiver Jalen Coker . Young also scored a touchdown of his own as a rusher.

Clearly, the Panthers still have some growing to do defensively, but you have to tip your hat to Bears head coach and offensive play-caller Ben Johnson—who's started out on the right foot in his goal to have the NFL's highest-scoring offense ever.

articles.body:
The final score between the Chicago Bears and Carolina Panthers has never happened before in NFL history. When we see an unprecedented score in an NFL game, it's called Scoigami . There haven't been too may times where a team scored 59 points, so that's a dead giveaway. The 59-37 final was the first time that has happened in NFL history.

Normally when we get a Scorigami, it's because something weird happened in the game like going for 2 or missed extra points. This one wasn't that. The Bears just laid the smack down. Chicago scored 14 points in the first, third, and fourth quarters along with a 17-point third quarter. Standard fare. We had a late extra point blocked, but 59-38 also has never happened.

We can expect a few more Scorigamis in 2026, but the Bears and Panthers started the new year with a bang.

articles.title: How long will Browns start Deshaun Watson at QB? The uncomfortable answer after Cleveland's blowout loss
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson got off to a horrid start to the 2026 season, but his leash as the starting Browns QB may be longer than you think.
articles.body:
It's going to be another long season in Cleveland .

That much is clear after watching a 34-10 blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1. The only question is what will be learned from the end before the next new beginning.

It was the same old sadistic setting in the first half. Quarterback Deshaun Watson threw an interception on the opening drive. Jacksonville jumped out to a 24-0 first-half lead behind Trevor Lawrence , who finished 18 of 23 for 245 yards and four TDs. Backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders paced the sidelines.

Watson – who is in the final year of a five-year, $230 million contract with Cleveland – finished 16 of 22 passing for 205 yards, one TD and one interception. He was sacked five times. First-year coach Todd Monken already has a quarterback question with an answer Cleveland fans aren't going to like in two weeks.

Who didn't see this coming besides everybody? Watson didn't play well in his first action since he suffered a torn Achilles tendon in Week 7 of the 2024 season. It's not about what is going to happen the rest of the season. It's what Cleveland will do in response that matters.

Simply put, Cleveland fans deserve better than this. Few fan bases can make that claim and mean it. The Browns traded Myles Garrett this offseason one year after he set the single-season record with 23 sacks. Watson was named the starter in the preseason after criticizing Browns fans.

Watson missed receiver Jerry Jeudy across the middle when he did not read linebacker Foyesade Oluokun underneath in coverage. Oluokun made a leaping interception. The Browns' next three drives resulted in a fumble and two three-and-outs. The Jaguars outgained Cleveland 23-495 and led 24-0 at halftime.

To put in perspective how bad that first half was – consider Cleveland's return to the NFL in Week 1 on Sept. 12, 1999. Pittsburgh had a 20-0 halftime lead in a 43-0 blowout. Which begs the question 27 years later: "What really changed?"

It's been a constant coach-and-QB matchmaking game with brief moments of success – including 2020 when Baker Mayfield led the Browns to the AFC divisional playoffs after beating the Steelers 48-37 in the AFC wild card round.

Lawrence was the No. 1 pick in the 2021 NFL Draft. Mayfield left Cleveland after the 2021 season. That's what it is. An endless series of what-could-have-beens when the reality on the field is barely watchable at times, and yet that fan base finds hope.

Raheim Sanders had a 74-yard kickoff return in the third quarter, and Cleveland pushed to the 2-yard line. A false start penalty stalled the drive, however, and they had to settle for a field goal. Watson completed a 25-yard crossing route to rookie KC Concepcion on the next drive, but that drop stalled in the red zone when Watson was sacked on third and fourth down.

Watson finally threw a TD on a 46-yard pass to second-round pick Denzel Boston with 1:52 remaining. That's one of those snippets of hope that probably confirms what will happen next for Cleveland – at least for this season.

Should Cleveland Browns start Shedeur Sanders at QB?

That last touchdown has meaning. Monken could have put Shedeur Sanders in with 4:39 remaining in the fourth quarter. Sanders finished 3-4 as a starter last season with 1,400 yards, seven TDs and 10 interceptions – numbers that were good enough to make the now-defunct Pro Bowl.

Sanders isn't a franchise quarterback, but he is inarguably a more popular choice among Browns fans – even if the results would not be that much better. Monken, however, likely will stick with Watson for the next few weeks – and that's going to be a test for all parties involved, including owner Jimmy Haslam and general manager Andrew Berry.

Cleveland plays Tampa Bay – led by Mayfield – in Week 2. Then comes back-to-back home games against Carolina and Pittsburgh.

Will Watson still be the starter after that stretch? Yes. Will the countdown to the quarterback-heavy 2027 NFL Draft begin in earnest? Yes. Is there reason to believe in a three-year plan that puts a more palatable product on the field when Cleveland's new stadium opens in 2029? That depends on whether the Browns can finally find that quarterback with some of the new young pieces such as Concepcion and Boston.

Cleveland fans have been waiting since 1999. Is three more years really that long?

articles.title: Horns Up for Dalton Kincaid in Buffalo Bills’ 36-31 win over the Houston Texans
articles.summary: The Bills are 1-0 after a big win over the Texans
articles.body:
What a way for the Buffalo Bills to open up the 2026 NFL season! Winning a back-and-forth affair against the Houston Texans —in Houston, no less—is a big accomplishment for a Buffalo squad looking to forge a new identity under first-year head coach Joe Brady. The Bills were able to lock in a victory for their new head coach, winning 36-31 for their first win at (now) Reliant Stadium since J.P. Losman led the team to a win back in 2006.

It wasn't all roses, though, and even if it were, Bret Michaels told us long ago that every rose does have its thorn. There were plenty of players deserving of their flowers, but there are definitely some areas for improvement after Week 1.

Our Horns Up and Horns Down are below. Let us know your thoughts about who and/or what stood out, in the comment section below! _____________________________________________________________________________

The newest addition to the Bills' offense was as-advertised today, making big plays in tight windows to give Buffalo's offense big yardage. Moore wasn't targeted until Buffalo's third possession, but he had a huge second quarter. He made his first grab on a deep post off a play-action pass, and he nearly caught his first touchdown later in the quarter on a deep ball from quarterback Josh Allen . However, safety Calen Bullock tackled Moore while the ball was in flight, and given that the foul occurred in the end zone, it gave the Bills a first down at the one-yard line. Moore eventually did catch his first touchdown later in the quarter, as Houston safety Reed Blankenship 's near-interception went into Moore's hands instead. Some fancy footwork kept him in bounds, and there was nobody around him to prevent him from finishing the 43-yard score. Moore caught three passes for 76 yards and that touchdown in the second quarter alone en route to a five-catch day for 100 yards and the aforementioned touchdown. Moore also had a team-high eight targets on the afternoon.

Buffalo's quarterback was exceptional this week. He scored two rushing touchdowns in the first half—one was a 21-yard scramble where he rolled right, found a lane, and dodged multiple defenders inside the five on his way to paydirt. The second was quarterback sneak where tight end Dawson Knox played the role of the schnowplow. Allen also threw the aforementioned touchdown pass to DJ Moore. The game plan featured some quick-hitters, but the protection pla up front helped keep Allen out of harms way for most of the afternoon. Buffalo chipped Houston's edge rushers with different players, and their varied personnel packages gave Allen clean looks against a top-line defense. Overall, it was the best day Allen's had in his career in Houston. He was efficient, he took checkdowns, he found big plays with his arm and with his legs, and he gave the Bills' defense a chance to win it in the end, and they obliged him. Allen completed 20-of-29 passes for 334 yards and two touchdowns, adding six carries for 23 yards and two more scores on the ground.

Buffalo's new-look secondary faced a strong test in trying to stop wide receiver Nico Collins , and they didn't do a particularly great job at it. Collins killed the Bills throughout the first half, catching all three of his targets for 46 yards and a score. Additionally, the Bills were called for far too many penalties in the secondary.

Safety Damar Hamlin and rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun were each called for a hold, and cornerback Christian Benford was called for pass interference. Hamlin's penalty erased a stop on 3rd & 9 that immediately led to a touchdown by running back David Montgomery . Later, Benford's penalty gave the Texans great field position at the end of the first half to set up a touchdown throw to Collins.

Granted, they mostly stepped up when they needed to on the final drive of the game, but there were too many instances of players losing their assignment. There are going to be growing pains on defense with a new system implemented by defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard , but the early returns were not great.

There were some encouraging early signs that the Bills would be able to bottle David Montgomery, but unfortunately, the much-maligned Houston offensive line was able to clear space consistently on the ground. Montgomery has always been tough to get on the ground, and Buffalo's stop unit had a tough time tackling today. Montgomery had touchdown runs of one yard and 18 yards in the first half, as he carried 13 times for 52 yards in the half. Woody Marks acted as a solid change-of-pace, as well. Montgomery had 60 rushing yards and two touchdowns, and he also added three catches for 19 yards and a receiving touchdown to his line. Marks had 36 rushing yards on eight carries, and while Houston averaged just 3.8 yards per rush on the day, it felt like they were able to gain the yards they needed in multiple clutch situations.

Buffalo was called for just too many flags on the afternoon. This has been a pattern so far this year, as the Bills were heavily penalized in the preseason, as well. A holding penalty on Sam Franklin Jr. wiped out a great kickoff return by Ray Davis at the end of the first half; Franklin Jr. was also whistled for a chop block early in the second half that negated a solid punt return from Greg Dortch . Dion Dawkins was whistled for holding, as was Alec Anderson , and the Bills even managed to commit ineligible man downfield penalties on consecutive plays in the first half. There were quite a few penalties in the game, as the teams combined for 17 flags and 191 penalty yards, so maybe there's an argument that second-year referee Alex Moore and his crew were a bit flag-happy. The fact remains, though, that Buffalo needs to be cleaner in its operations moving forward.

Buffalo's top tight end made some big plays for his quarterback in scramble-drill action. He hauled in a 38-yard pass in spectacular fashion right before the two-minute warning in the first half. Then, he made his second grab of the day on a third-quarter scoring drive, sticking with Allen on a rollout to find a nine-yard gain between two Texans defenders. He found space for big gains on a second field goal drive in the second half, and he also made the key reception off a play-action pass to set up Joshua Palmer 's go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter. Overall, Kincaid notched five catches on six targets for 130 yards in what was an incredible first game of the 2026 season for him.

The Bills forced two turnovers, and both of them came on strip-sacks of C.J. Stroud from Groot. On Houston's first possession of the game, Rousseau came around the edge and took the ball from Stroud, forcing a fumble that Ed Oliver (who had a good game himself) recovered. On Houston's final possession, Rousseau strip-sacked Stroud once again, bringing a third-down play to an end when linebacker Terrel Bernard , who also had a game-high 12 tackles on the afternoon, recovered it. Rousseau had four tackles and five quarterback hits to go with his two strip-sacks, but perhaps the most impressive play he made all afternoon came in coverage against tight end Dalton Schultz . The big tight end ran an angle route off the edge, and Rousseau, who has converted to a stand-up outside linebacker after having played defensive end for his whole career, not only stuck with Schultz, but he laid out and broke up the pass.

Not to be outdone, the big fella in the middle was a massive headache all afternoon. Walker commanded constant double-teams, and he often shed them by flinging very large men off of him in the way that most of us mere mortals might flick a fly off our arm. Walker had six tackles, two tackles for loss, and one tremendously important sack on the play immediately prior to Rousseau's game-ending strip-sack on the final drive of the game. One of the major defensive bright spots that I saw involved the four-man rush plan from Buffalo, as the big boys up front really did a nice job holding their lanes and using each other on stunts and games. That's a positive to build on in what was otherwise a less-than-stellar defensive effort today.

Welcome back, No. 16! Bass made all of his kicks, including three field goals and three extra points. His long on the day came from 46 yards, but the most impressive kick he had was his final field goal. Reid Ferguson 's snap was high, and rookie punter Tommy Doman Jr. did a great job corraling it and putting the ball down. That was the kind of thing that could have easily thrown off the operation, but Bass stayed locked in and he nailed the kick to give the Bills a 30-28 lead in the fourth quarter. He won't be perfect all seaosn, but it was nice to see him come out and have a perfect start to his 2026 season after missing all of 2025.

Who do you want to talk about, folks? The floor is yours after a big-time win to open the 2026 season. Go Bills!

articles.title: NFL Week 1 Winners and Losers: Bears' offense looks every bit as good as Ben Johnson said it would be
articles.summary: The Bears are going to have a lot of high-scoring games this season.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson said he wants his team to be the highest scoring offense in NFL history .

Based on the season opener, it might happen.

The Bears offense was just as impressive as Johnson said it would be in a 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers . Caleb Williams had a fantastic game, including as a runner. He had two touchdown runs. One was a 29-yarder, which tied the longest run of his career. Williams had 269 yards and two touchdowns asa passer and 65 yards as a rusher. The Bears rushed for 291 yards as a team.

Nearly everyone got involved as the Bears put up 552 yards and almost 60 points. Kyle Monangai had a 61-yard touchdown. He and D'Andre Swift both had 100 yards rushing. Williams threw touchdowns to Cole Kmet and Jahdae Walker , who are far from the Bears' biggest stars. Everything clicked. The Bears went off despite a catch-less game from tight end Colston Loveland , who should still have a big season in Chicago's offense. It just wasn't his turn on Sunday.

Johnson is so confident in his offense, he went for it on his own 21-yard line in the first half. The Bears didn't get it. The offense made sure it didn't matter.

Still, there are some things to clean up. The Bears started with a 31-point first half. The defense started by giving up 31 points in the first 36 minutes of the season. The game was tied 31-31 with 9:02 left in the third quarter. You can expect a lot of Bears games to look like that this season. Bryce Young ended up with 361 passing yards and three touchdowns. And the Bears won by more than 20.

The Bears' offense is tremendous. Nobody questioned that coming into the season. What was in doubt was if the defense could keep up. Last season the Bears survived a mediocre defense by leading the NFL in turnover margin by a wide margin. That's hard to replicate. But in the end, the Bears defense did enough to win and that's what matters. They'll win plenty of games in which they give up a lot of points, like Sunday.

The Bears won the NFC North last season. And from the first glance, it looks like the offense is even better. If nothing else, every Chicago game will be a wild ride.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 1 of the NFL season:

Lamar Jackson : Jackson was the first-team All-Pro quarterback in 2023 and 2024. He was hurt in 2025 and everyone seemed to forget how good he was.

Jackson is great when he's healthy, and it didn't take long for the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback to show it. He had a 5-yard rushing touchdown to start the Ravens' scoring, and there was a flood of it after that. Jackson had 321 passing yards and 40 more rushing. Zay Flowers had 150 first-half receiving yards, though he left the game with a hamstring injury. Derrick Henry looked good too, with 144 rushing yards and three touchdowns. The Ravens had 31 points in the first half. They beat the Indianapolis Colts 41-23.

The Ravens need Jackson to stay healthy, and they need their receivers to be healthy too. Flowers could be a big loss. But Baltimore's defense looked pretty good in Jesse Minter's first game as head coach. And, no surprise, Jackson looked like he could be an MVP candidate again.

Josh Allen : The Houston Texans still could have the NFL's best defense this season. Allen carved it up.

The Texans gave up their most points since the 2023 season as Allen went off in a 36-31 win. The Bills defense clinched the win with a strip sack of C.J. Stroud in the final seconds.

Allen gave the Bills the lead with 1:36 left with a 34-yard pass to Joshua Palmer on third-and-11. That avoided a long Tyler Bass field goal attempt with the Bills trailing. It also came after Allen caught a break when his wild throw to the end zone was almost picked off, but dropped. Allen had 334 yards and two touchdowns, with two touchdowns rushing.

The Texans' defense will be fine. Allen was just that good on Sunday.

Detroit Lions , but barely: The Detroit Lions won, but they can't be too happy about how they played.

The Lions didn't look great, but they held on to beat the Saints 31-30 in overtime. They forced an incompletion on a two-point conversion as the Saints went for the win.

The Lions had just a touchdown in the first half, though the defense was doing its part. An interception and a fumble recovery early in the second half turned a 7-0 game into a 21-0 lead for Detroit. But the Saints rallied as the Lions defense started to get ripped apart. A touchdown from Tyler Shough to tight end Juwan Johnson in the final two minutes tied a game that the Lions once led by three touchdowns at home.

The Lions scored first in overtime but New Orleans answered with a Noah Fant touchdown. Shough ended up with 410 yards and two touchdowns. The Saints went for the two-point conversion and the win, but the Lions defense got the stop it needed.

Even though the Lions defense came up big with the one play it needed to win, it will have to be better going forward. In four days, they face Josh Allen and the Bills.

Mike McCarthy: McCarthy got the call to go home to Western Pennsylvania and lead the Pittsburgh Steelers as Mike Tomlin's replacement as Pittsburgh Steelers head coach. His first game was a success.

The Steelers will face tougher opponents than the Atlanta Falcons , who were down to their third quarterback in Cooper Rush because of injuries, and Pittsburgh will need to play better than they did Sunday. The game was a little too close against a depleted Falcons team, and a defensive touchdown on an interception by T.J. Watt saved the Steelers in a 20-13 victory. A win is a win and the Steelers will be happy to start 1-0.

McCarthy has a lot to live up to, because Tomlin always at least dragged Pittsburgh to a .500 record when he was coach. Avoiding a loss to the Falcons is a good start.

Bumbling Buccaneers : The Tampa Bay Buccaneers were one of the NFL's worst teams in the NFL over the second half of last season. They lost seven of eight games after their bye before winning the finale, but it wasn't enough to win the NFC South, one of five divisions in NFL history to have a champion with a losing record.

The bad vibes continued Sunday. The Cincinnati Bengals took advantage of many Buccaneers mistakes in a 33-27 win. Their first touchdown came when Myles Murphy stripped Baker Mayfield and Bengals linebacker Demetrius Knight Jr. scooped the fumble and scored. Three of the first four Buccaneers possessions ended with a fumble, including Mayfield fumbling at the Bengals' 4-yard line. They lost four fumbles in all, three by Mayfield.

The Buccaneers played well enough to win. Despite all those mistakes, they lost by just six points on the road. But they did make those mistakes. Just like the second half of last season.

Cam Ward : If Ward can't have a decent outing against the New York Jets at home, is it going to happen at all this season?

Ward's preseason struggles carried over to the regular season. He and the Tennessee Titans looked awful in their season opener against a Jets team that was 3-14 last season. The Jets won 23-10. Ward was 19 of 32 for 140 yards.

Ward came into this season with some pressure to be better than last season, when he was the No. 1 overall pick and struggled. He largely got a pass for a horrible rookie season because he was in a bad situation. That situation improved. In the season opener, Ward didn't.

Deshaun Watson and the Browns: Watson's first drive of the 2026 season ended with an interception. Everyone could see that coming, except the Browns.

It doesn't matter if Watson can get the team in and out of the huddle OK and he might know the offense better, because he is not a viable NFL quarterback anymore. Don't tell the Browns that, however. They started him even though it made no sense from any angle, other than perhaps that was their way of tanking. The Browns lost 34-10 to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1, and it never felt that close.

The Browns trailed 24-0 at halftime of their opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Trevor Lawrence is a real NFL quarterback and he had three touchdowns in the first half. Watson had 75 yards at halftime, 91 fewer than Lawrence. Watson finally had a nice play when he threw a deep touchdown to Denzel Boston, but it came with 1:52 left in a 34-3 game. It was a stark contrast: The Jaguars are pretty good, and the Browns can't get out of their own way. Just remember, the Browns voluntarily made Watson their QB1 to start the season.

articles.title: Josh Allen finally overcame Texans in Houston, leading Bills to dramatic last-minute victory
articles.summary: In a matchup of expected AFC heavyweights, the Bills beat the Texans, 36-31, as Josh Allen and the Bills drove 96 yards in just over 90 seconds to take the l...
articles.body:
Josh Allen had the ball with a chance to force overtime or win in his previous two games against the Texans in Houston . Both times, he and the Bills came up short in close losses.

In Week 1 against his familiar foe, in a stadium he'd lost all four games he's played in his career, Allen was determined to end that streak.

In a matchup of expected AFC heavyweights, the Bills beat the Texans, 36-31, as Allen and the Bills drove 96 yards in just over 90 seconds to take the lead with 1:36 remaining. Allen hit Joshua Palmer — on his only catch of the game — for a 34-yard TD strike.

Allen overcame near disaster when he threw a ball up for grabs late, and the Texans' Kwame Lassiter dropped it in the end zone. One play later, Palmer beat Lassiter for the touchdown.

Buffalo's defense, which was on its heels most of the game, came up with the big stop on the final possession, sacking C.J. Stroud twice — and recovering his fumble on the second one.

Allen finished the game 20-of-29 passing for 334 yards and two scores. He also ran for two first-half TDs, including a wild, 21-yard scramble late in the second quarter.

D.J. Moore had five catches for 100 yards and a TD in his Bills debut, and tight end Dalton Kincaid had a career-high 130 yards on five catches.

Throw out a 40-0 win by the Bills against a Texans team that went 4-13 in 2021, and Allen had struggled badly in his career against the Texans, with the Bills losing all four of their games in Houston.

The first two meetings came early in Allen's career, including his playoff debut. Allen hadn't yet become the superstar we know him to be. Both were excusable losses.

The last two, in 2024 and 2025, were tough losses. Allen had the ball in both games with a chance to tie and force overtime or win. The Bills came up short in both. Allen didn't play well in either, completing 9-of-31 passes in the first one and taking eight sacks and throwing two picks in the second.

Allen wasn't perfect Sunday, but he was close. Considering the opponent, it was a marquee showing.

The Bills turned the ball over on downs on their first possession, with Allen stuffed on a fourth-down run, and they settled for a field goal (after a turnover deep in Houston territory) on their second. But the Bills finished out the half with three straight TD drives and took the lead into halftime.

The Texans kept storming back, taking the lead twice in the fourth quarter in a game that featured eight lead changes. Allen led scoring drives after both to deliver a signature victory for a Bills team that — like the Texans — harbor legitimate Super Bowl belief this season.

This Texans defense entered this season with the reputation of being a top-three unit in the NFL — their unquestioned superpower. Allen ripped through them most of the game Sunday in Joe Brady's debut as head coach.

Moore wasn't targeted until there were less than five minutes left in the first half, but he had a productive day, which included drawing a 46-yard defensive pass interference call that set up Allen's second rushing TD.

But the most promising development was Kincaid having a career day. He hauled in receptions of 35, 38 and 40 yards — all massive receptions that helped fuel Bills scoring drives.

The 2023 first-rounder had been a disappointment to this point on the whole, especially when it came to injuries. He missed a combined nine games then past two seasons and reportedly played through a PCL injury last season that clearly limited him.

If Allen has a healthy Kincaid available this season, it could add an extra dimension to an offense that had lacked downfield prowess. On Sunday, Allen completed five passes for 34 yards or longer. Doing it against an elite defense spoke volumes.

articles.title: Lions avoid collapse, narrowly beat Saints in overtime after blowing a 21-point lead
articles.summary: The Saints clawed their way back from a 21-0 deficit in the second half.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions are walking away from Week 1 with a win, but it took a lot more effort than anyone expected. After blowing a 21-point lead, Detroit found a way to force a key stop at the last second against the New Orleans Saints in overtime to pick up the 31-30 win .

It literally came at the last possible second, as the Saints opted to go for two after scoring an overtime touchdown with just 1:34 left to play to make it 31-30.

Saints quarterback Tyler Shough , who had converted a number of tight throws on the drive previously, couldn't find a receiver in time, forcing the final throw just a little too far out of the corner of the end zone to lose game.

To that point, Shough and the Saints had shown a ton of fight in the second half and overtime. After coming back from 21-0 and nearly winning the game on a 62-yard field goal in regulation, the Saints looked as though they would rally again after an overtime touchdown by Amon-Ra St. Brown finally got the Lions back on track .

The Saints attempted to answer back, with Shough converting multiple difficult throws on the final drive of the game. Chris Olave and Juwan Johnson , in particular, came up with massive catches to extend the drive and give the Saints a chance to win the game.

After a Noah Fant touchdown narrowed the lead to a point, Saints coach Kellen Moore decided to go for two and end it. The Saints' pass catchers and Shough just couldn't come up with one more clutch conversion to win it all.

The Lions seemed comfortable leaning on the running game early, getting Jahmyr Gibbs a ton of action in the first half. But the Saints' defense played things close, limiting the Lions to just seven points at halftime thanks to a Gibbs run.

Coming out of halftime, though, the Lions finally seemed to find their stride. Another Gibbs score and a touchdown catch by Amon-Ra St. Brown put Detroit up 21-0 with a little under nine minutes to play in the third quarter.

At that point in the contest, Saints quarterback Shough had turned the ball over three times — two interceptions and one fumble. It looked as if the Saints were done.

Somehow, New Orleans found a way to rally. After the Lions went up 21-0, the Saints scored on their next drive, cutting into the lead. The Saints then forced a three-and-out and scored again, making it a one-score game in the fourth quarter.

After both teams traded field goals, the Saints faced a seven-point deficit with just 2:32 to play. Shough found himself in a some trouble early on the drive, but eventually hit Olave with a 42-yard pass to get the Saints down to the nine-yard line.

Olave, in particular, turned in a huge performance, finishing the contest with 10 catches and 182 yards in the loss.

On the next play, Shough hit tight end Juwan Johnson to tie the game 27-27.

The Saints were able to stop the Lions and turn in one more drive before the end of the game. The team even managed to drive the ball down the field enough to force a 62-yard field goal as time expired. Daniel Carlson 's attempt sailed wide, sending both teams to overtime.

The Lions finally snapped out of their second-half malaise on their first drive of overtime, but still needed a last-second stop to come out ahead against the feisty Saints.

articles.summary: With new head coach Robert Saleh in town and Cam Ward entering his second, the Tennessee Titans seemed due for a year of growth.
articles.body:
With new head coach Robert Saleh in town and Cam Ward entering his second, the Tennessee Titans seemed due for a year of growth.

One game into the 2026 campaign, that doesn't seem to be the case. The Titans opened their season with a 23-10 loss to Saleh's former team, the New York Jets.

Ward failed to get much going under center, and he said he was "very disappointed" by his performance.

"Those are some big plays that we could have had, but we still got a lot of things to clean up for sure," Ward told reporters . "I'm very disappointed. We're better than what we showed offensively. We trained a lot this offseason. We had some hard days. It didn't pay off for us today, but it's going to pay off for us eventually, whether it's next week or the week after, but we're going to get it rolling, and it's exciting."

Ward completed 19 of his 32 pass attempts for 140 yards and a touchdown, adding 21 yards on the ground. His biggest issue was accuracy, as the former No. 1 overall pick missed a handful of receivers on what would have been big plays.

Saleh brought in former New York Giants head coach Brian Daboll as the Titans' offensive coordinator, which led to high expectations for Ward, but it's clear the 24-year-old still has a long way to go.

Ward and the offense's poor performance led to boos from fans in Nashville.

"It doesn't make me feel any type of way. The fans come here for a show," Ward said. "They spend their money to come see the Titans win games, and we want them out here each and every day."

A performance such as Sunday's could lead to big changes for a team trying to rebuild, but Saleh emphasized that he won't make any emotional decisions after a rough first game.

"I think everyone's a little frustrated," Saleh said. "Don't confuse my calm demeanor with frustration, but before I blurt and start screaming, I'm going to watch tape and try to make sure that we make rational, educated football decisions to make sure that we're putting our players in the best position to be successful. Same thing with our players. I can throw podiums around if you want to make everyone feel good. But it's really go back, watch the tape, figure it out and see if we can get better from this."

Things don't get any easier next week as the Titans face the Philadelphia Eagles. Unless Tennessee turns things around dramatically in the next week, the team will be on its way to a 0-2 start for the third consecutive season.

articles.title: Acrisure Stadium witnesses NASA’s 1st official flyover during football game
articles.summary: The Steelers’ first game of the 2026 NFL season featured the first official NASA flyover at a football game.
articles.body:
The Steelers' first game of the 2026 NFL season featured the first official NASA flyover at a football game.

A pair of T-38 Talons from NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston buzzed over Acrisure Stadium at the game's start Sunday.

Astronauts use those supersonic jets in their flight readiness training.

NASA Flight Director Anthony Vareha told Channel 11 that Pittsburgh is a great city to grow up in if you're interested in space.

"This is a great place that inspires curiosity and inspires wonder," said Vareha, himself a Pittsburgh native. "And you can take that launching pad, like I did, and it carried me all the way to Cape Canaveral and the Johnson Space Center where I'm one of the flight directors for all of our space missions."

The flyover was part of NASA's effort to build excitement for the next Artemis mission, slated for next year ahead of a planned moon landing in 2028.

articles.title: NFL Weekend Review: Josh Allen's box office finish, Trevor Lawrence's MVP contention and Derrick Henry greatness
articles.summary: The NFL Weekend Review guides you through the best of the action from across the league on the road to Super Bowl 61 in Los Angeles; watch the Kansas City Chiefs against the Denver Broncos in Monday Night Football, live on Sky Sports NFL from 1.15 Tuesday
articles.body:
The Josh Allen experience is back with a vengeance. Perennial thrill, unyielding adventure, eternal tenterhooks - the knife-edge epitome of everything we've so dearly missed about this wonderful game called football.

The Buffalo Bills quarterback positioned himself front and centre to a box office finish on the NFL's opening Sunday of the 2026 season, flirting with catastrophe before playing hero just seconds later to lead his side to a 36-31 win over the Houston Texans.

Kamari Lassiter should have iced the game for Houston inside the final two minutes when Allen gift-wrapped a would-be interception to the Texans cornerback, who failed to hold onto the ball while back-peddling in his own end zone. How quickly he learned not to grant Josh Allen a second life.

On the very next play Allen would connect with Joshua Palmer for a 34-yard touchdown on third-and-11 to put Buffalo on top with 1.36 remaining. Jim Leonhard's new-look Bills defense handled business from there, Greg Rousseau forcing a fumble from CJ Stroud and Terrel Bernard pouncing on the loose ball to call game in the final seconds.

The camera quickly panned to Allen's beaming smile on the sidelines as the Bills quarterback resumed the never-ending Super Bowl quest that continues to dictate the pre-season, in-season and, such has been his playoff agony, post-season narrative. Every year is his year, until it isn't, yet the vicious cycle never fails to convince us that his Lombardi lift is just around the corner.

It is moments like Sunday that reinforce the concept, Allen's association with the dramatic fuelling Buffalo's unwavering contention with him at the helm. The Texans had been purring with fresh optimism, their offence hanging in a shoot-out with what is consistently one of the league's best units, C.J. Stroud going toe-to-toe with Allen, until the latter had seen enough.

It is daggers like Sunday's, and closing moments like those, that define Allen - underlining an ability to strap a team to his back in a manner few other quarterbacks in the league can attest to. He is back like never before, piloting a side determined to cash in on his prime this offseason by firing Sean McDermott and subsequently replacing offensive coordinator Joe Brady with a new head coach.

Allen finished Sunday 20 of 29 for 334 yards and two touchdown passes to Palmer and newest receiver DJ Moore, while also rushing for two scores to lift his career tally of ground scores to 81.

The Bills are coming off their fourth divisional-round defeat in five years following January's loss to the Denver Broncos, having also been beaten at two AFC Championship Games since 2020. It stands as the NFL's biggest modern door-knocking venture. But Allen is back, and he just took down one of the most feared defenses in the league.

The Los Angeles Chargers remain one of the most frustrating teams in football, and flattered to deceive yet again as they began a season of promise in defeat. Jim Harbaugh's side fell to a 26-14 defeat to an Arizona Cardinals team led by Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, the early marriage of Justin Herbert and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel failing to generate the fireworks expected of it. Their depth at receiver beyond Ladd McConkey is unconvincing for a team with playoff ambitions and what had been a transformed defense under Jesse Minter feels short on game-changing pass rush disruptors.

The Chicago Bears have the offensive firepower to hurt and hang with the best in the NFL as Ben Johnson seeks to solidify his team as permanent Super Bowl contenders. Chicago scored their most points in a game since the 1980 season as they beat the Carolina Panthers 59-37 in the highest-scoring opening game in NFL history, in doing so amplifying their rising star quarterback and one of football's most dynamic rushing schemes. Caleb Williams reminded all of his credentials with a precision-perfect back-shoulder fade touchdown pass to Cole Kmet on his way to 269 passing yards and two scores, while D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai both put up 100 yards rushing.

David Montgomery gives the Texans a new dimension. The question surrounding Houston heading into this season was whether CJ Stroud and their offense could reach a level capable of rewarding a Super Bowl-calibre defense. It proved it could be by going stride-for-stride with Josh Allen and the Bills, Montgomery shining with three touchdowns having arrived in a trade from the Detroit Lions in the offseason.

Bijan Robinson has a long season ahead. I'm not sure there is a more glaring example of an offense so heavily reliant on one player performing well in order to operate. Atlanta's quarterback problems are not going away anytime soon, you feel, and Sunday was an insight into how prominent Robinson will be in Kevin Stefanski's attack as he recorded 29 touches for 173 yards and a touchdown in scrimmage in the Falcons' 20-13 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Trevor Lawrence is an MVP contender. Sure, the Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback was playing an incompetently run Cleveland Browns team, and sure, he was facing a defence adjusting to life without Myles Garrett and Jim Schwartz. But there had been a sense coming into this season that the NFL still wasn't universally sold on the Lawrence-Liam Coen tandem. Based on Week One, Lawrence has picked up exactly where he left off at the end of a glittering second half to last season.

The former No 1 pick finished 18 of 23 for 245 yards and four touchdowns in Jacksonville's 34-10 victory, extending their winning streak to nine straight regular-season games dating back to the 2025 campaign. Coen continues to inspire the most assured, clinical and surgical version of Lawrence the NFL has seen.

Browns defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg said his unit would be built on violence and bad intentions. That might have been an overreaction, because they barely got close enough to the Jags' play-caller to find out.

Dalton Kincaid : The Bills' tight end dazzled in a career-best performance in which he caught five of his six targets for a team-leading 130 yards, and came up with fourth-quarter catches of 40 and 35 yards respectively - an invaluable contribution to the Bills' thrilling win.

Jalen Hurts: The Eagles quarterback has his critics and will seemingly forever divide opinion over his place among the best quarterbacks in football, but it was Hurts who willed Nick Siranni's team to victory on Sunday. He wasn't pretty, nor was he perfect, but he showed his composure in the face of pressure once more to throw for three touchdowns in a 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders.

Carson Wentz: This wasn't in the script. The Minnesota Vikings were forced into an early quarterback change against the Green Bay Packers when Kyler Murray exited with a concussion. In came Carson Wentz to lead Kevin O'Connell's offense, throwing for 133 yards and three touchdowns to stun the Packers in a 39-22 rout.

Baker Mayfield: Four days after signing a three-year, £121.9m contract extension with the Buccaneers, Mayfield fumbled the ball three times in his side's 33-27 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, including once in a scramble on the Bengals one-yard line - a mistake that effectively cost his team the game in an encounter decided by a single score.

Cleveland Browns : The Browns' rebuild project has looked larger by the week - and their humiliating 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars further highlighted the size of the task at hand.

Quarterback Deshaun Watson - playing his first regular season game since October 2024 - was mediocre at best, his only touchdown coming in garbage time, and Cleveland's defence allowed Lawrence and his offence to score on six of their first seven drives.

Tennessee Titans : A home opener against an inexperienced New York Jets side was about the kindest fixture the Titans could have asked for to start their season - and even that proved too tall a task for the 2025 NFL's basement side. Head coach Robert Saleh fell victim to the side that sacked him in 2024, and 2025 No 1 pick Cam Ward failed to impress once again, managing just 140 passing yards.

Player of the Weekend - Derrick Henry, RB, Baltimore Ravens

The Baltimore running back - dubbed by team-mates and fans alike as 'King Henry' - added another regal flourish to his illustrious career with an incredible week one performance.

Henry notched 144 yards and three touchdowns from his 24 carries in the Ravens' 41-23 road drubbing of the Colts, moving him to third on the NFL's all-time rushing touchdowns list with 125, passing hall-of-famers Marcus Allen and Marvin Harrison.

At 32, Henry continues to redefine conventional ideas about his position, breaking records at an age that far surpasses the average running back's ability to continue playing in the NFL, let alone do it at the league-leading standard he performed at in the season opener.

History beckoned in both directions. The New Orleans Saints were threatening their biggest comeback win ever, and the Detroit Lions were threatening their biggest blown lead in franchise history having surrendered a 21-0 lead to find themselves locked at 24-24.

It would be Detroit who survived humiliation as they clinched a 31-30 win in overtime after Tyler Shough's pass fell incomplete on the two-point attempt.

Shough had sent the game to overtime with a nine-yard touchdown strike to Juwan Johnson with 1.07 remaining in the game, before the Lions struck in the extra period thanks to Amon-Ra St Brown's four-yard touchdown catch. But back came the Saints as Shough fired an eight-yard scoring strike to Noah Fant, before Kellen Moore elected to go for the win instead of the game-tying field goal.

Second-year quarterback Shough had been enduring a miserable start to his second before finishing 35 of 56 passing for 410 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions, Chris Olave his chief target with 10 catches for 182 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs, the highest-paid running back in NFL history, starred for the Lions with 29 carries for 156 yards and two touchdowns.

The big news from Sunday came before kickoff as it was reported Myles Garrett will miss at least the next four weeks due to a knee injury that requires surgery.

The Los Angeles Rams pass rusher has been placed on injured reserve in an early disruption to his first season with the Rams after arriving in a blockbuster trade from the Cleveland Browns earlier this year.

Garrett was quiet on his debut for the team during the week as Sean McVay's side suffered a 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne.

The Vikings were dealt an injury setback later in the evening when starting quarterback Kyler Murray suffered a concussion in Minnesota's 39-22 win over the Packers.

The former Cardinals quarterback received a huge hit on a third-and-seven scramble in the first quarter, his helmet coming off as he came into contact with Lukas Van Ness and Javon Bullard. He eventually returned to his feet and was able to walk to the locker room, before being replaced by Wentz.
